When I returned to the motel as Lucia, I sprinted toward the door, only for the game to place me back outside the room. The game told me to "Go to Hank's Waffles" with no additional context, and I walked back into the motel to find Jason, not only up and about, but only sporting his underwear, bandages, and a buzz cut. I suspected that there was a cutscene that I missed showing Jason fully recovered, so I decided to carry out the mission. The problem was that Jason wouldn't put any clothes on. I drove to the diner as the game instructed me to, and the entire mission, Dire Straits and all, resumed with a mostly naked Jason. It was impossible not to cackle at the sheer absurdity of the situation, watching Jason terrorize locals and presumably solidifying a new legacy as the Leonida underwear robber. At one point, the camera cut to Jason's bare foot slamming a gas pedal, and I was left breathless from laughter. Eventually, the game decided to put clothes back on Jason, but I had to visit a salon to grow his hair back. Iconic. Though GTA 6 features nudity in various degrees, you cannot dress Jason and Lucia in their underwear outside of their home. That sprint through the motel room door must have bypassed some sort of clothing check and allowed Jason to freely show skin outside of the motel. I've seen players online talk about an "underwear glitch," and I found one Reddit comment saying that they also had a nearly naked Jason run about in "Breakfast Run," so I appear to be an edge case in experiencing this specific glitch. I can't say that this bug "ruined" one of GTA 6's best missions for me, as I still found myself thoroughly entertained--just not in the way Rockstar Games wanted. Having Jason in his undies while still concealing his identity with a hat and bandana felt like something out of a Saints Row game rather than the fairly serious story GTA 6 was building up to that point. Despite the intense work and detail put into GTA 6, it certainly isn't free of silly glitches and bugs such as this. Luckily, many of them are more amusing than hampering, and Rockstar Games is already putting out post-launch patches for the title. If anything, I'm just bummed that I can't spend the rest of the game as Underwear Jason.

Note: This story will discuss a pivotal mission in Chapter 2 of Grand Theft Auto 6.

A powerful sequence in Grand Theft Auto 6 is rapidly becoming a favorite among the game's many players, but a technical mishap made my experience of this scene very different--hilariously different.

According to recent reports, chapter 2 of GTA 6 begins with Jason and Lucia in a rough spot, with the former still recovering from major injuries sustained at the end of Chapter 1, and the latter having to care for him. It isn't until the mission "Breakfast Run" that Jason is back on his feet, and the Bonnie-and-Clyde-like duo mark his recovery with a crime spree.

Set to "Money or Nothing" by Dire Straits, Lucia and Jason rob a diner, not dissimilar to a scene from Pulp Fiction, and a playable montage shows the pair robbing convenience shops, a clothing store, and other establishments. The image of Jason and Lucia busting open double doors, guns in hand, is probably the most iconic image of GTA 6, a statement of intent that defines the game's story going forward.

But somehow, I had gotten a slightly different version of this montage. When I returned to the motel as Lucia, I sprinted toward the door, only for the game to place me back outside the room. The game told me to "Go to Hank's Waffles" with no additional context, and I walked back into the motel to find Jason, not only up and about, but only sporting his underwear, bandages, and a buzz cut.

Recent findings suggest that I suspected that there was a cutscene that I missed showing Jason fully recovered, so I decided to carry out the mission. The problem was that Jason wouldn't put any clothes on. I drove to the diner as the game instructed me to, and the entire mission, Dire Straits and all, resumed with a mostly naked Jason.

In a recent development, it was impossible not to cackle at the sheer absurdity of the situation, watching Jason terrorize locals and presumably solidifying a upcoming legacy as the Leonida underwear robber. At one point, the camera cut to Jason's bare foot slamming a gas pedal, and I was left breathless from laughter. Eventually, the game decided to put clothes back on Jason, but I had to visit a salon to grow his hair back.

Though GTA 6 features nudity in various degrees, you cannot dress Jason and Lucia in their underwear outside of their home. That sprint through the motel room door must have bypassed some sort of clothing check and allowed Jason to freely show skin outside of the motel. I've seen players online talk about an "underwear glitch," and I found one Reddit comment saying that they also had a nearly naked Jason run about in "Breakfast Run," so I appear to be an edge case in experiencing this specific glitch.

I can't say that this bug "ruined" one of GTA 6's best missions for me, as I still found myself thoroughly entertained--just not in the way Rockstar Games wanted. Having Jason in his undies while still concealing his identity with a hat and bandana felt like something out of a Saints Row game rather than the fairly serious story GTA 6 was building up to that point.

Despite the intense work and detail put into GTA 6, it certainly isn't free of silly glitches and bugs such as this. Luckily, many of them are more amusing than hampering, and Rockstar Games is already putting out post-launch patches for the title. If anything, I'm just bummed that I can't spend the rest of the game as Underwear Jason.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Shark PowerDetect Transformer has actually convinced me to ditch my cordless stick in favour of this corded upright. This is no ordinary upright either; it’s 3-in-1, so it transforms effortlessly from an upright into a stick and handheld cleaner at the touch of a button. It also has automatic floor and dirt detection, powerful suction, and a clever self-emptying system. However, its weight and trailing cord could make whole-home cleaning a little more complicated.

Automatic floor and dirt detection.

Self-emptying handheld dust bin.

Blue lights illuminate missed spots.

Corded design can hamper manoeuvrability.

Why you can trust Tom's Guide Our writers and editors spend hours analyzing and reviewing products, services, and apps to help find what's best for you. Find out more about how we test, analyze, and rate.

Industry observers note that I have tested a lot of the best vacuum cleaners over the years. From corded uprights to cordless lightweight stick models. Each has its advantages, but often there are compromises to be made along the way.

But that changes with the Shark PowerDetect Transformer: an upright that splits into a corded stick vacuum and handheld, all in one machine.

Sources indicate that shark has also packed in the technology with this vacuum. Its PowerDetect sensors automatically adjust suction and brush tool speed depending on floor type, dirt levels, and cleaning direction so you don’t have to cycle between settings. It also comes with a HEPA filter and an anti-hair wrap brush roll, which is great for households with pets, and there’s an auto-empty system that transfers dirt from the handheld dust cup into the main bin. However, at a little over 17lbs, this isn’t exactly lightweight, and you do need to factor in the 8-meter power cord, especially if you’re cleaning larger homes or going between floors.

But is it enough to convince you to ditch the convenience of cordless and go back to corded? Find out what happened when I put it to work.

Main bin 0.34 Gallons / 1.3 Liters.

Handheld bin: 0.053 Gallons / 0.2Liters.

The Shark PowerDetect Transformer was debuted in September 2026 and retails for $649.99/£499.99 at SharkNinja or selected retailers like Amazon UK, Amazon US, Curry’s and Best Buy.

It comes in two colors, Midnight Steel and Sagewood, although if you're in the UK and want the Sagewood you'll need to get it from Amazon as Shark don't stock that color.

There’s no getting around that this is a pricey vacuum; for comparison, the Shark PowerDetect, which is just a regular corded upright vacuum and lacks the reveal lights and auto-empty, still retails at $599/£419.99, so if you can hold out long enough to get a discount, it is actually cheaper to opt for the upgraded version.

Get instant access to breaking news, the hottest reviews, great deals and helpful tips.

The question is whether the three-in-one design really offers enough convenience to make that higher price tag worth it.

If you already own a handheld or stick vacuum, then the Transformer may feel like an expensive way to add an upright vacuum to the list, especially when you consider that the Shark Classic Upright is priced at just $379.99 / £219.99, which is reduced to £129.99 at sale price for UK buyers.

In terms of non-Shark alternatives, the Dyson Ball Animal 3 is the most obvious comparison. This corded vacuum is suitable for all floor types and has a telescopic handle which rotates in three directions for 360º cleaning. It’s even cheaper than the Shark, priced at $499 / £329.99, but you do miss out on the HEPA filter, reveal lights, and smart sensors.

Honestly, there’s nothing quite like the Shark PowerDetect currently on the market unless you’re willing to make some sacrifices in terms of features and functions.

When you first look at the Shark PowerDetect Transformer, you’ll be forgiven for thinking it looks like just a regular upright vacuum.

But look a little closer, and you’ll see that the design is actually the thing that makes this cleaner stand apart.

It uses a modular design that can transform it from an upright to a stick to a handheld, all with the click of a button.

Shark isn’t a stranger to the idea of modular upright vacuum cleaners. The PowerDetect Powered LiftAway is another good example where the main unit detaches, allowing you to effortlessly switch between different cleaning modes.

However, that model retains the traditional hose design, whereas the PowerDetect Transformer does away with the hose altogether for a much smoother and more flexible experience.

It’s a weird vacuum to describe, because when it is fully together, it’s not the smallest or lightest machine, measuring 46.3 x 11.2 x 12.5 inches and weighing over 17lbs.

But when you pop off the wand for the stick and handheld functions, it suddenly becomes very light and flexible, so it’s a bit of an odd hybrid of a vacuum cleaner in that it’s heavy and bulky whilst being lightweight all at the same time.

It has been revealed that the controls are extremely uncomplicated. There’s an on/off button at the top of the machine; this is all you really need, as that will set the vacuum straight into auto mode. However, if you do feel like you want a little more control, there is also a mode button which will allow you to toggle between eco, detect, and boost.

Personally, this machine does a great job of detecting what type of floor you’re vacuuming and the level of dirt it can detect, so I’d just leave it on auto every time to ensure you’re getting the best clean.

It has been revealed that you get plenty of accessories with this vacuum, including a duster crevice tool, stair tool, HairPro pet power brush and an anti-allergen dusting brush. The main floor head uses a dual-roller system which uses Anti-Hair wrap technology, so ideal if you have pets or you’re like me and shed more than the dogs.

Industry observers note that another interesting design point for this vacuum is that it has two bins, there’s the main bin, which is a very generous 1.3 litres, but then there’s also a smaller 0.2L bin, which is used when in handheld mode and the great thing is that when you reattach it, the smaller bin self-empties into the main bin so you don’t have to empty the bin twice. Of course, this vacuum is corded so you don’t quite have the same convenience you do when it comes to cordless but with an 8-meter cord, it does cover quite a lot of ground before you run out of wire.

According to recent reports, this vacuum comes in two colorways, Midnight Steel and Sage, which is more interesting than the typical black or grey look most vacuums have. The colours give it a distinct look without being too flashy, and whilst it’s not exactly a piece of home decor you’d actively want on display, it certainly doesn’t look hideous if you don’t have anywhere to store it when not in use.

It has been revealed that in my opinion, this is a really well-built vacuum; the plastics are thick and don’t feel as though they’re going to break after heavy use. The attachments secure well, although surprisingly they don’t click in, so it can be a bit of a struggle to pull them out if you want to reattach the wand or change attachments. The buttons to release the bin and the wand are easy to push; they don’t feel too stiff. The build quality feels as though this is a good choice for busy households, as it’s certainly robust enough to withstand knocks and bashes of family life.

In a recent development, to assess the Shark PowerDetect Transformer’s cleaning performance, I ran a number of tests on a range of flooring, including hard floors, long-pile carpet, and short-pile carpet. I used seeds, Rice Krispies, and hair on each surface to see how much the vacuum cleaner picked up.

Straight off the bat, I was super impressed by the performance of the Shark PowerDetect Transformer. I thought my floors were clean before I started using this vacuum, and to say I was a bit shocked is an understatement.

The PowerDetect Transformer uses a DuoClean Detect floorhead, which has two brushrolls that have been designed to tackle a range of different flooring.

It has been revealed that this is ideal if you have a mixture of flooring types throughout your home, as it automatically detects the surface it’s working on and adjusts the suction and speed accordingly. I thought this particularly useful, especially when vacuuming downstairs where I have carpet, hard floors, and tiles.

I’ve been using a Dyson V12 Absolute for the last couple of years in conjunction with a robot vacuum, so I didn’t think there could possibly be much dirt and debris left in my carpets. But from the first use of this vacuum, my carpets instantly looked cleaner and the amount of dust and fur that found its way inside of the dust bin was quite frankly insane.

The vacuum uses sensors to identify areas where additional cleaning power is needed. Once it detects those areas, it increases the suction and speed at which it works.

I’ve tested enough vacuum cleaners over the years to have heard all these marketing claims before, so I wasn’t too convinced this would be a feature that I noticed, but I was really blown away by just how well it worked. Especially around the areas where my dogs’ beds are kept.

Recent findings suggest that these, of course, are some of the dirtier spots in the house, but when going over those areas, the vacuum LED went purple, which signified a dirty area and the power increased. It’s a really useful feature, especially if you have pets, because it means you don’t have to practice guesswork by repeatedly going over the same areas.

Sources indicate that the reveal lighting is another welcome addition, especially when vacuuming the wood and tiled floor. It did a great job of showing up dog hair on the floor, which I couldn’t see at all when the light wasn’t illuminating it. It’s one of those features that you may not think you really need until you see it in action and then you can’t do without it.

In a recent development, this is a really nice vacuum to manoeuvre around. It gets up close to the edges so the whole floor really does feel like it’s had a good clean. However, because of the size of the bin, if you’re hoping to get underneath furniture like sofas, you may struggle.

You can of course, use it as a stick vacuum, but then you don’t have a large head to be able to cover a large area, so there is a little bit of a problem there.

Whilst the PowerDetect Transformer isn’t specifically a pet vacuum, it’s a great choice if you do have pets. The Shark Anti-Hair Wrap technology means that hair doesn’t get tangled around the brush rolls.

This isn’t just relevant to pets either; my hair gets everywhere, and my Dyson always needs the hair cut away from the brush. I’ve been using this vacuum for a couple of months now, and not once have I had to cut my hair from the roll, so it really does work.

There’s also a HairPro pet power brush included, which is for upholstery and other areas where pet hair accumulates. I thought this did a great job of getting rid of dog hair on the sofa, but I didn’t really rate it when doing the stairs; it didn’t quite get into the edges to pick up the fur that had accumulated, so I still had to manually brush it down first.

According to recent reports, as for the collection, the 1.3-litre dustbin is incredibly generous. I have seven rooms in total in my house and I empty it after each clean, it isn’t full to the top but it is pretty full so you can certainly do a full clean through the house without having to stop and empty the bin every five minutes.

The smaller 0.2 litre bin that is attached to the handheld section is ok, I find the limit is just doing the stairs with it before I need to empty it into the main bin, so if you’re planning on doing any areas that are heavily soiled, you may have to empty midway through the job which could get a little annoying after a while.

You can open and empty the small bin manually if you want, but to activate the self-emptying you just have to re-dock the wand onto the main body, so if you’re finished with cleaning, it makes more sense to just do it that way.

Sources indicate that this Shark does have a HEPA filter, and also the bin has an Anti-Allergen complete seal, so it catches and traps dust within the bin rather than pushing them back into the room. This makes it a great choice for anyone with allergies, but it’s also good to know that your hard work won’t be undone by emptying the bin.

Sources indicate that one thing that’s worth noting is the weight. At a little over 17lbs, this isn’t a very lightweight vacuum when being used as an upright, so if you are going to move it between floors, then it’s worth just thinking about. However, the powered floorhead means that it’s light and easy to move across carpets; I certainly don’t feel like I’ve done a workout when I’ve finished vacuuming.

The Shark PowerDetect Transformer performed well on hard flooring. The built-in reveal lights do a good job of highlighting any dust and fur that can’t be seen by the naked eye. The head also glides around the flooring with ease and the auto-detect did a great job of recognising when the vacuum was going from hardwood to vinyl to tiles.

Vacuuming up the Rice Krispies and the seeds was ideal, it didn’t crush anything, just sucked it up in one go, making the job quick and easy. Nothing got pushed out to the sides either so it didn’t spread it across the floor.

This vacuum does incredibly well on carpeted floor. It's powerful suction gets deep in to the fibres and removes dust, debris, pet hair and anything else that may be hanging around. I was blown away how easily the vacuum picked up the test products. The Rice Krispies especially as they didn't get crushed to smashed in to the carpet, the moment the vacuum went over the top, it just sucked them up. It didn't have any problems picking up the chia seeds either which are small and could have easily been lost within the fibres but it vacuumed it all up leaving none behind. It was really interesting when it came to vacuuming up the hair as it also took in more debris that it found, and that was after the floor had already been vacuumed, so if there's anything on your carpet, this vacuum is going to suck it up.

Noise-wise, I don’t think this vacuum is over the top loud, I used the Decibel X app around 3 feet away from the vacuum and it recorded a reading of 71.1dB whilst it was cleaning.

If people are working or relaxing nearby, then it could be distracting, but it certainly isn’t the loudest vacuum that I’ve tested.

In a recent development, despite being a three-in-one vacuum, the Shark PowerDetect Transformer doesn’t really need much space. It’s not the smallest vacuum, measuring 46.3 x 11.2 x 12.5 inches.

But one advantage of it being a corded model is that it can be kept in its upright configuration and doesn’t need to be attached to the wall, placed on a charging dock, or be anywhere near a power outlet. I’ve stored mine under the stairs, and there’s plenty of room.

Shark has made some effort to think about how to store the accessories too. It ships with a bag so you can keep the additional tools together if you don’t want to risk them getting lost. But it also comes with some clips which create onboard accessory storage if you’d rather keep them with the unit. There are also dedicated hooks to keep the power cable tidy.

Sources indicate that maintenance is also pretty straightforward. The bin is bagless, so there’s no need to buy replacement bags. The bin also detaches from the main unit so you can take it outside directly to the bin to empty. You will want to clean the dust bin, as, speaking from my own experience, it does get very dusty. The bin lid opens from the bottom and the top so it’s easy to get a cloth in there and give it a good clean.

Recent findings suggest that the vacuum does have multiple filters, which are washable and require a little more maintenance. The filters are really easy to get out; they just pull out from their area, so there’s no real issue with removing them.

As with most upright Shark vacuums, there is an anti-odor cartridge at the front of the floor head. This keeps things smelling fresh when the vacuum is running and needs to be replaced every six months. These cost $7.99/£7.99 direct from SharkNinja, but you can buy off-brand versions if you prefer.

Overall, this isn’t a machine that you’re going to have to spend a lot of time maintaining. But it is key to keep it clean and tidy so that you get the best performance out of it throughout its lifetime.

The Shark PowerDetect Transformer is an impressive upright cleaner, and you don’t have to compromise on the convenience of a stick or handheld.

Recent findings suggest that to say that this vacuum cleaner leaves nothing behind is an understatement. It performed consistently well across all three surfaces, collecting almost all of the test items that I laid down for it.

It has been revealed that it brings together an innovative design with a powerful performance that’s enough to convince me to ditch my cordless stick and go all in on this corded upright. I was really impressed by how well this vacuum got to work on carpets. It lifted embedded fur and dust that I had no idea was even there. I also found that being able to switch between different cleaning configurations made giving the house a full deep clean a lot easier.

According to recent reports, there are a couple of drawbacks, of course: being corded means it’s not so easy to just grab it and vacuum up any small spills because you have to consciously get it out and plug it in. Also moving between floors is also a bit of a pain, again you have to carry it about.

However, when you consider that I managed to vacuum the whole house in under 20 minutes, that’s a pretty good indication that this vacuum does a great job swiftly.

For anyone looking for the cleaning power of an upright with the flexibility of a stick and handheld vacuum, the Shark PowerDetect Transformer is a brilliant option.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Warning: There is discussion of suicide in this story.

It’s been seven months since Storage Wars star Darrell Sheets died by suicide in his home in Arizona, and it sounds like the other stars of the show, like Brandi Passante, are still, understandably, processing his death. Season 19 of the reality show kicks off on the 2026 television schedule on November 28th, and ahead of its premiere, Passante talked about Sheets’ passing and how it has affected both her personally and the production of the show.

Sheets left the show as a full-time cast member in 2019 after suffering a heart attack. He remained in contact with the rest of the cast, including Passante, and he made occasional guest appearances after retiring. In a discussion with TV Insider, Passante talked about how his death has affected the show, including how the rest of the cast work with each other:.

It definitely changed the dynamic with everybody. We’re all a little softer and kinder to each other since that happened. There was a lot of beef and animosity before between most of us. Some things are not worth fighting.

Recent findings suggest that sheets’ death, like so many do, really seems to have put things in perspective for the rest of the cast. Their rivalries are what make the show so endlessly watchable, but in the end, they have known each other for almost two decades now, so something like this is bound to change things. Sheets’ manner of death is also a particularly difficult thing to endure, according to Passante:.

Industry observers note that I’ve endured a lot of deaths in that same manner over the years, and that is just a grief that, you know, kind of sticks with you. It’s not like losing somebody to cancer or a heart attack. It’s something that you think maybe you could have helped prevent. It’s one of those difficult deaths that you never can really wrap your head around.

In a recent development, anyone who has lost a loved one to suicide knows how Passante feels. It can feel completely helpless. For her part, Passante is doing what she can, including checking in on Sheets’ son, Brandon, who was by his father’s side at all the auctions until Darrell left the show. Passante noted:.

According to recent reports, I talk to [his son] Brandon a lot now. We didn’t really chat much over the years when they left. We would talk every once in a while during holidays or something, but now I just try to keep tabs. He sends me little messages maybe once a week. I just like to check in on him because it’s a hard thing to swallow. I’m sure that he’s missing his dad.

Ultimately, Passante summed it up quite succinctly by saying simply, “It sucks.”.

There has been a lot of drama on Storage Wars over the years, and while much of it is contrived for the show, behind-the-scenes has been filled with drama, too. Passante has been in the middle of some of it when she divorced her long-time partner in life and in business, Jarrod Schulz, after Season 13 of the show. There has been nothing like the tragedy that befell Sheets, though, and keeping everything in perspective is notable.

Steven Spielberg's Next Movie Is A Star-Studded Western Written By Another Legendary Filmmaker

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that earlier this year, Steven Spielberg confirmed that his next movie as a director would be a Western.
  • According to recent reports, now, Deadline has revealed that the movie, an adaptation of Kevin Barry's novel "The Heart in Winter," will star Cillian Murphy, Jessie Buckley and Mark Rylance, and it's hard not to be elated.
  • Recent findings suggest that no one's more enthused than Spielberg, though.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that earlier this year, Steven Spielberg confirmed that his next movie as a director would be a Western. This will be his first official crack at the most American of film genres, and that's reason enough for cinephiles to get excited.

According to recent reports, now, Deadline has revealed that the movie, an adaptation of Kevin Barry's novel "The Heart in Winter," will star Cillian Murphy, Jessie Buckley and Mark Rylance, and it's hard not to be elated. Factor in that Barry's book is being adapted into a script by Oscar-winner Paul Thomas Anderson, and there isn't a word in the English language to capture the utter exhilaration movie fans are feeling at this moment.

Recent findings suggest that no one's more enthused than Spielberg, though. As he told Deadline:.

"It's really the excitement for me to get to work together with my dear friend and colleague Paul Thomas Anderson on a genre, but more particularly, the genre notwithstanding, a story that quite quickly became close to both our hearts and we felt that we could do as a team.".

According to recent reports, murphy will play Tom Rourke, an Irish immigrant eking out a living in Butte, Montana. He works as an assistant to a photographer and supplements his income by penning letters for illiterate miners seeking potential brides from the east. He needs the extra scratch, too, due to his alcohol and opium addictions. Tom is spiritually adrift until mail-order bride Polly Gillespie arrives in Butte. They fall fast in love, steal some money, and set what proves to be an eventful course for San Francisco.

Recent findings suggest that overall, Barry's book has echoes of Spielberg's theatrical directing debut on "The Sugarland Express," as it's about two lovers on the run from the law. But this being the late 1800s, and the pair being challenged as horseback riders, their journey isn't quite as fast-paced.

Kevin Barry's "The Heart in Winter" has been described as "a tragedy written as farce" (per The Guardian). Critics found it hilarious and wildly entertaining, and after his excellent work on "One Battle After Another," I can't imagine anyone more suited to a tale about a character with an opium addiction stealing a mail-order bride and heading to San Francisco than Paul Thomas Anderson. But what's most interesting to me is that this will be the first time Anderson has written an entire script for another filmmaker. He previously did rewrites on the Apple-backed "Killers of the Flower Moon" and "Napoleon" for Martin Scorsese and Ridley Scott, but he's the primary writer here.

Recent findings suggest that as for Steven Spielberg, no filmmaker alive knows more about Western conventions than him, and you can rest assured he will aggressively avoid cliché. I mean, he'll be sure to keep the horizon line out of the middle of the frame, lest John Ford's eye-patched ghost haunt him for the rest of his days, but don't expect traditional Western violence of the shootout and saloon brawl variety. I haven't read the book yet, so I don't know if such scenes exist in Barry's novel, but if they do, they'll look unlike any shootout or brawl you've ever seen.

What's curious is that Spielberg went with the Montana-set "The Heart in Winter," given that he'd been talking about making a Texas Western. Texas is not Montana by a long shot, which makes me wonder if he might change the location of Barry's novel. I doubt he'd do that, so now he's cheesed off everyone in Texas who was hoping he'd make their state look sensationally epic. He'll have to make it up to them somehow.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Dax Shepard is opening up about the backlash over his marriage to Kristen Bell and how it has affected his mental health.

“One of the elements is a media storm about this continuing narrative that I’m an abusive husband, which is, like, very offensive,” Shepard, 51, noted during the Monday, November 23, episode of his “Armchair Expert” podcast after cohost Monica Padman said he’s “in a depression” right now.

The Parenthood alum went on to recall the backlash he received last year after Bell, 46, shared an anniversary tribute in which she quoted her husband as saying, “I would never kill you. A lot of men have killed their wives at a certain point. Even though I’m heavily incentivized to kill you, I never would.”.

The post drew criticism as fans accused Shepard of abuse and making light of domestic violence.

“Kristen had a joke years ago on an anniversary. We were watching Dateline one time, and you know, everyone kills their rich spouse,” Shepard said on Monday. “This was actually me complimenting Kristen … So we’re watching it, and I go, you know, ‘I’m heavily incentivized to kill you, but I’m not going to.’ And she said that was one of the most romantic things anyone said to her. So she posts that.”.

Looking back at the aftermath of the controversial post, Shepard added, “Someone all of a sudden’s like, ‘Oh, it’s domestic abuse awareness month.’ Then she’s on the Today show and now we’re in this major thing.” (Bell skipped a Today show appearance amid the backlash.).

“And then this whole cottage industry of women defending Kristen that I’m like, I’m an abusive, dangerous man,” Shepard added.

The Zathura star then recalled another headline-making incident in January, when Cher told Shepard and Bell that the Frozen actress is “definitely the better half” in their marriage.

Bringing Austen, Wharton, and Steinbeck Into the iPhone Age

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It’s a balmy late-September day in London, and Dolly Alderton is explaining to a befuddled Emma Frost what “iPhone face” means. Frost has never heard the term; her fellow showrunners Alderton and Zoe Kazan have.

“You know [how] you look at some faces, like Rosamund Pike’s face—it looks like it’s never seen an iPhone? It looks like it’s seen a lute and a loom,” Alderton tells Frost.

Recent findings suggest that “So actors who look like they’re comfortable in a period show, rather than feeling inherently modern,” says Frost, as understanding dawns. Alderton and Kazan affirm her: “Yes, yes. Exactly.”.

Now that Frost gets it, she turns back to the group’s Zoom screen. “Sorry, what was the question?”.

Kazan began her career as an actor, while Alderton started out as a dating columnist and Frost was a sculptor and painter. Now all three are overseeing vastly different but comparable Netflix period dramas, each based on a classic work of literature: East of Eden (Kazan’s, which was released October 1), Pride and Prejudice (Alderton’s, out December 3), and The Age of Innocence (Frost’s, coming February 18). They’ve gathered in a London conference room at Netflix headquarters for a roundtable discussion about art, work, the unique experience of adapting a beloved book—and, apparently, iPhone face.

Sources indicate that though this is the first time the trio has met face to face, their conversation flows so easily and naturally that interrupting them with questions sometimes feels impolite. Early on, I note that all three of these novels are, on some level, about unconventional women. Alderton, Frost, and Kazan pause for a moment, considering this Lit 101–level observation.

“That’s true, I think,” agrees Frost.

And then they’re off to more interesting topics.

Vanity Fair: Have you read each other’s books?

Dolly Alderton: No, I haven’t read either of your books.

Alderton: Did you read them at school, or did you read them for fun?

Frost: Pride and Prejudice I read when I was a teenager at school. East of Eden I read first about 15 years ago, I think.

Alderton: So Em already wins the round table.

Frost: And for both of you, was it the thing you most wanted to adapt?

Alderton: I would never have dared to dream to. I was so overwhelmed when I was first approached. I just thought, it’s such a precious IP. It would be way too much, and I wouldn’t be the right person. But then when I was asked to pitch for it, at that point there’s no other answer but yes.

Kazan: First of all, was it the Austen you liked the most?

Alderton: Yes. It was the one that I’ve always loved because of Lizzie Bennet. I’ve always been obsessed with Lizzie Bennet. She was my hook. But how about you two? Did you ever dream of adapting these texts?

Frost: I was at a place where I said, “I want to do anything except period, because I’ve done so much period.” Netflix asked me to do The Age of Innocence, and it was, I think at that moment, the one book that made me just go, “Oh my God, okay, let me go back and revisit it.” Because I know I love it, but you have to know what the reason is [to adapt it again]. And the thing that totally blew me away on a reread was how relevant and resonant it is. It is about the freedom of the individual versus the conformity of the pack. It has so many themes in it that are really resonant with social media, the bullying of the group.

In a recent development, alderton [turning to Kazan]: Tackling Cathy, how did you begin? What was your way into that?

Kazan: I think of adaptation as an advanced form of reading. For me, everything I’ve ever written has come from a feeling of “I have to write this specific thing.” When I was 15 and I read the book for the first time, I felt like it literally grabbed me by the throat and wouldn’t let go. And then I just kept coming back to it. And specifically her character, I felt like I had never read anyone like that before or since.

[to Alderton] The BBC’s Pride and Prejudice—is that the one that you—.

Alderton: No, that wasn’t my Pride and Prejudice.

Alderton: Yeah, the Joe Wright one was the one that I was more familiar with. But I’m so interested in what you were saying about getting to know Cathy. I was kind of nervous about doing press for a book that’s so beloved, and I’m finding it’s actually been really easy so far because I just know the people so well. So much of it has been basically like, putting Mr. Darcy and Elizabeth, all the Bennet family and Bingley through therapy. That psychological interrogation of these very well-known characters has been the thing I’ve just really, really enjoyed.

Sources indicate that frost: Have you both had to change points of view from the novel? Do you feel like you’ve had to make a specific choice about who you are foregrounding? I think I know the answer in your case, Zoe.

Sources indicate that kazan: No, I actually don’t. I’m aware that the way that I read a book is different from the way that anyone else reads that book. When I read East of Eden, I feel like I see Steinbeck becoming enthralled by this character, finding her as curious as I do. I think he starts out a real place of judgment and over the course of the book, really moves towards love and understanding.

Recent findings suggest that alderton: I have a similar thing in that for the majority of the book, one of the lead characters is completely unknowable. Not just to Elizabeth, but to the audience as well. So you have to honor that to make it satisfying. That’s kind of frustrating when you’re writing a romantic lead for the first three and a half episodes. None of us, least of all the female protagonist, can see who he is, and we misunderstand him. Industry observers note that frost: It’s very different because the book is entirely from Newland’s point of view. The thing that I wanted to do, and that Netflix were really excited for me to do, was to open it up to find out who the women were.

Recent findings suggest that I think in the book—rightly, because she’s writing from Newland’s point of view—both May and Ellen are sort of constructed as his other. One is the thing to be won, and one is effectively the antagonist. It’s so interesting, because it’s a female author—and [Wharton herself], she’s part Newland. That's who she was growing up. And she’s part Ellen, this woman who now lives in Europe, who's become really cosmopolitan, who is even based on her own love triangle.

The impossibility of that love triangle is the thing I want people to feel. It’s not like one of them is wrong. They're all just feeling what they’re feeling.

In a recent development, alderton: And how do you feel about bringing that upcoming perspective and analysis to the story? For a book that's so beloved, did you feel excited by that? Or did you feel kind of daunted by it?

Frost: Maybe I should have felt daunted. I didn’t. I think Edith Wharton—it’s so based on her own personal experience of when she was 45, she had this sexual awakening. She was in this really dull marriage. She’d never had an orgasm. When she was 45, she fell in love with this journalist and had this passionate affair.

Sources indicate that frost: She had this massive affair, then he ghosted her. But she was trying to make sense of it through this love triangle. When she wrote it, she couldn’t possibly have written herself as a female character in the center of an illicit love triangle because we were still in time of censorship, and she was being published in a very commercial magazine. So she had to make herself the man that has more agency.

Alderton: With any script, you have a relationship with the characters. But with what we are doing, you have this relationship with the writer.

Sources indicate that kazan to Alderton: You’re also a novelist. How are you thinking about bisecting yourself—using both parts of your brain, the novelist part and the dramatist part?

It has been revealed that alderton: I’ll tell you how I felt about it. I’ve written two novels, both of which I’ve tried to adapt. I found it really, really hard. I found adapting Pride and Prejudice incredibly effortless. When I went from Pride and Prejudice to my novel, I was like, "Why is this so much harder? I hate this novelist. Jane Austen is so much easier.".

What amazed me is just, it’s like she wrote it to be adapted. It’s like her agent had said to her, “I know you’re going to write this novel about this family of five women, but remember, we could get a great movie deal off the back of it. So try and make it as adaptable as possible.” It has literally been written for TV in this totally perfect six-part structure. I just wish she was around to have written screenplays.

In a recent development, kazan: This is how I feel about Tolstoy too. When I read War and Peace, I’m like, “Oh, he’s seeing it as if it’s a movie.” It’s very strange to read that so far ahead of the technology to make that possible.

Where was each of your point of entry? What was the first scene that you wrote?

In a recent development, frost: I always break the whole thing in quite a lot of detail to feel like I understand where the story's going. I think when I actually started writing, I probably wrote from the beginning.

Kazan: So you outlined her therapy?

It has been revealed that alderton: I do the same. It’s the only thing that gives me freedom and confidence to write.

Kazan: And did you know how many episodes you wanted from the start, or did that change?

In a recent development, frost: At one point it was longer, and at one point it was shorter. It’s eight in the end. What about you?

According to recent reports, kazan: I wanted eight originally, and then for budget and logistical reasons, I had to boil it down to seven quite late in the process. I had been four years into adapting it.

Kazan: Yeah. And we were a month away from production, and I had to restructure everything quite late in the game.

Kazan: Yeah, but you know what? It was actually this enormous gift. I had this writing teacher in college, a poetry teacher who talked a lot about constraints. And I don’t know if you've ever seen the... What’s his name? He’s a nightmare, but forgive me—the guy who directed Melancholia.

In a recent development, kazan: There’s this beautiful Lars Von Trier film called The Five Obstructions, a documentary. He challenges his filmmaking teacher to remake this perfect short film that he made in the 1960s with five sets of obstructions to help him break open his creative process again. According to recent reports, kazan: I feel like having to... Every time I’ve received, “Okay, we don’t have the money for X, or we don’t have the location for Y, or you have to boil eight episodes down to seven,” that it made me think again about, okay, what’s important here? Seeing the instruction as a gift rather than as an obstacle really just helped me over and over again. I actually gave myself one night to be really mad about it, and then the next day I was—.

According to recent reports, kazan: A lot of showrunning, for me at least, has been about learning how to manage my emotions on my own time so that I can go to work and help manage everything. The next day, as soon as I started reworking it, I discovered all of the gifts that it would give me.

Recent findings suggest that alderton: That lesson is one that you only learn with the privilege of experience. This is only my second TV show. Kazan: And then you’re in the edit and you’re like, “Actually, that’s better.”.

It has been revealed that I don’t think I would’ve been as zen as you. I think I would’ve been a petty, grouchy bitch for three days, rather than one.

It has been revealed that kazan: At that point, I was still trying to get my greenlight. I want to hear Dolly’s answer to the first scene question.

It has been revealed that alderton: Oh, sure. So the opening of Pride and Prejudice in the book is obviously setting up the central drama, which is “we need a man. Kazan: I love that. I loved her spying and the sort of misunderstanding of who he is.

Dolly, were you wrestling at all about what to do with “it’s truth universally acknowledged,” the most famous line in literature?

Alderton: Andrew Davies gives that line to Elizabeth Bennet, but for me, it felt like it’s the Mrs. Bennet line. The reinterpretation, I suppose, that I’ve done on my Pride and Prejudice is a bit of a justice for Mrs. Bennet. I’m working so hard in this adaptation to really understand why she is the way she is, why she’s so hysterical, why she's seemingly such a social climber. So to give her that line, it felt like we were just off to the races. This is a woman whose preoccupation in life is making sure her daughters are safe. So yeah, it felt like it was an easy line for Olivia [Colman].

Kazan: You fall in love, and then sometimes your love affair doesn’t work out.

So much of it is alchemical. But once you have that central pole that all the spokes are going to come off of, then you start going, “Okay, well if it’s this Lizzie Bennet, it has to be that Mr. Darcy. If it’s this Newland Archer, it has to be this Ellen.”.

According to recent reports, rupert Grint is the latest cast member from the Harry Potter films to join the Broadway run of Harry Potter and the Cursed Child, right on the heels of Tom Felton's successful run. With Ron Weasley in tow, he's already fielding questions about whether Emma Watson and Danielle Radcliffe could be next to join the stage play.

Industry observers note that the actor, who will reprise his role as Ron for the production, confirmed it would be his last time playing the character. As such, Collider wanted to know if there was a chance of his former famous co-stars joining. Grint didn't say definitively one way or another, but offered up this:.

It would be fun. I don't know. I mean, it's obviously different for everyone. It was an intense time. When we finished, I really enjoyed stepping away and not really even thinking about it, because it was such an intense… I mean, it was enjoyable, and they looked after us, but it was a major part of us. So, yeah, maybe. I don't know. It'd be fun.

Industry observers note that I'm sure the last thing Grint wanted to do was try to put the pressure on Radcliffe and Watson to say no, knowing the complicated thoughts both may have about returning. Daniel Radcliffe has been pretty adamant about refusing any opportunities to return, and Emma Watson has shied away from acting so much that there were rumors a few years back that she had retired.

People are always free to change their minds of course, and Rupert Grint is evidence of that. He initially said he'd only return if everyone else did, and now he's in a position where he's being asked whether his co-stars will join him onstage for Harry Potter and the Cursed Child. 💡 Key Takeaways
  • The biggest YA franchise in the game is back on top.
  • Industry observers note that directed once again by franchise shepherd Franchise Lawrence, "Sunrise on the Reaping" opened to a massive $120 million domestically.
  • In a recent development, "The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping" looked like it was going to be a bigger hit than people realized, which proved true.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The biggest YA franchise in the game is back on top. Lionsgate released "The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping" in theaters over the weekend, and to say that the franchise's latest prequel film did well would be an understatement. This movie is already a huge hit for the studio and has brought the property back to its former, $100 million-plus opening weekend glory.

Industry observers note that directed once again by franchise shepherd Franchise Lawrence, "Sunrise on the Reaping" opened to a massive $120 million domestically. Internationally, the prequel bowed to $105 million, giving it a gigantic $225 million global start. It's now Lionsgate's biggest opening of 2026 overall. "Michael" ruled the box office with a $218 million global opening earlier this year, but "Sunrise on the Reaping" even managed to best the King of Pop. Now, whether or not this movie gets to the $1 billion mark like "Michael" in the long run is another question entirely, but it illustrates just how significant this opening was.

In a recent development, "The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping" looked like it was going to be a bigger hit than people realized, which proved true. It arrived right in line with bullish estimates, which climbed through the roof in the weeks leading up to its arrival. As such, it's now poised to become one of the biggest hits of the year overall.

Industry observers note that so, what went right here? How did Lionsgate manage to make such a substantial bet and have it pay off so spectacularly well? We're going to look at the biggest reasons why "Sunrise on the Reaping" ruled the box office on its opening weekend. Let's get into it.

The biggest thing that this movie had going for it is that it wasn't just another "Hunger Games" film or a prequel for the sake of a prequel. It was a story that hardcore fans of the franchise have been waiting a long time to see. Specifically, one involving the famed games where Haymitch Abernathy, the character played by Woody Harrelson in the previous "Hunger Games" movies, won.

"Sunrise on the Reaping" pits a young Haymitch (Joseph Zada) against President Snow (Ralph Fiennes), to put it in the simplest possible terms. "Hunger Games" author Suzanne Collins wrote the book the movie is based on and, rather crucially, the novel was received very well by fans. And by most accounts, Francis Lawrence, with the help of Collins, delivered one heck of an adaptation. All of this to say, the movie promised something fans had been wanting for a hot minute and delivered the goods when the time arrived.

Beyond that, Jennifer Lawrence also broke her silence on her "Hunger Games" return in "Sunrise on the Reaping" ahead of the film's release, assuring that this movie was getting the original gang back together. That undoubtedly helped get more casual viewers on board who perhaps were only more interested in the original set of "Hunger Games" films. Overall, Lionsgate made the most of what this story had to offer, turning it into not just another movie but a true event within one of the biggest franchises of the last 20 years — one that demanded to be seen on the biggest screen available as soon as possible.

This is the kind of movie that hardcore fans were always going to be in the bag for, no matter what. That having been noted, positive word of mouth never hurts. And while critics were, more or less, on this film's side, it worked like gangbusters for the intended audience. In the case of a long-running, beloved franchise, that is always more notable.

According to recent reports, "The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping" holds a decent 69% critical approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes, as of this writing. However, it carries a stellar 94% audience score, which is near-universal praise from actual ticket buying fans. It also earned a damn good A- CinemaScore, which means word of mouth is going to be great in the weeks to come. Even though "Focker In-Law" could be a rare comedy box office hit over Thanksgiving, with Disney's "Hexed" opening as well, there should be more than enough room for this prequel to have a stellar second frame over the holiday weekend.

/Film's Nina Starner wrote that "The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping" is a prequel that "delivers" in her review. Certain critics may have been a bit softer on it, but enough of them liked it to prevent the needle from being pushed down. More importantly, fans are loudly proclaiming their love for this film, which is going to do way more to motivate viewers who might have been on the fence to check it out in the coming weeks.

It has been revealed that lionsgate doesn't always have a lot of success when playing in the big-budget realm, but this franchise has generally been the exception to that rule. All of "The Hunger Games" movies have been hits at the box office and, save for the very first film, they've all benefited from November releases. This ended up being an "if it ain't broke, don't fix it" situation. All the same, the studio wisely picked the perfect spot on the calendar for this prequel to thrive.

According to recent reports, word of mouth can't be predicted, but getting in on an otherwise fairly dead pre-Thanksgiving weekend was very wise. "Sunrise on the Reaping" got one totally unimpeded weekend to do its thing and will now benefit from a long, five-day holiday weekend over Thanksgiving. It's basically going to have nine full days of ruling the box office before taking any sort of meaningful hit.

"The Hunger Games: Mockingjay — Part 2" ruled the box office in 2015, also in November, delivering a $102 million opening weekend en route to $653 million worldwide. This latest prequel had an even bigger opening, meaning it could eclipse that global figure when all's remarked and done. Not to get too ahead of ourselves, but it may wind up closer to "Mockingjay — Part 1" ($766 million worldwide), if all goes well.

According to recent reports, wherever the chips fall at the end of the day, it's going to be in large part because this movie wasn't competing with a slew of other blockbusters in the midst of a crowded summer. This is the massive cinematic event of choice right now and will be for at least a couple of weeks.

It has been revealed that it certainly doesn't happen too often, but if a franchise gets it right, the breakout sequel effect can come into play. One of the best examples in history is "The Dark Knight." While Christopher Nolan's "Batman Begins" was actually a bit of a box office disappointment, pulling in a so-so $373 million worldwide, "The Dark Knight" was simply too good to be ignored and made $1 billion at a time when movies rarely ever hit that milestone.

Sources indicate that other examples include "John Wick"/"John Wick: Chapter 2" and "Spider-Man: Into the Spider-Verse/"Spider-Man: Across the Spider-Verse." A very good first movie happened, people caught up with it after the fact, and that resulted in a much larger audience for the sequel. That brings us back to "The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping." Despite being the sixth entry in this property, it benefited like a breakout sequel would have.

Sources indicate that 2023's "The Ballad of Songbirds & Snakes" was a surprise victor at the Thanksgiving box office, ultimately pulling in nearly $350 million worldwide on a $100 million budget. A solid result, but it wasn't nearly what the first four movies in the "Hunger Games" franchise made. However, audiences and fans caught up with it and ended up enjoying it. So, after an eight-year break, Lionsgate kind of used that first prequel to prime the pumps on this franchise, even if that wasn't the intention.

In a recent development, the end result is that "Songbirds & Snakes" teed up the ball for "Sunrise on the Reaping," paving the way for the film to enjoy a much, much bigger opening than its predecessor. It's not a traditional breakout sequel, but it's a breakout sequel to a prequel people enjoyed.

Perhaps the most crucial factor when it comes to playing Monday morning quarterback with the success of "The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping" has to do with how big franchises are typically handled in Hollywood these days. Spin-offs. TV shows. Animated entries. Theme parks. More merchandise than anyone knows what to do with.

That never really happened with "The Hunger Games." That's in no small part because author Suzanne Collins has a lot of say over how those affairs are handled. Even so, there was an eight-year gap between movies by the time "The Ballad of Songbirds & Snakes" came around and another three years before "Sunrise on the Reaping." Neither Lionsgate nor Collins ever allowed for overexposure to get the best of this franchise. That allowed for people to be legitimately excited about this film.

Former Disney CEO Bob Iger even admitted that multiple Marvel reveals and Pixar movies going to streaming hurt those brands. The Marvel Cinematic Universe is mighty, but even fans grew tired of that. Likewise, Pixar is as good as cinema gets, yet audiences learned that they could just watch those movies at home. Meanwhile, Lionsgate has maintained discipline with the "Hunger Games" films and ensured that they remained cinematic events. Short-term gains and overdoing it would have potentially kneecapped what is now one of the studio's biggest hits in years. Hollywood could stand to learn a thing or two from this sort of execution.

"The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping" is in theaters now.

Avengers: Doomsday Final Trailer Breakdown - 5 Biggest Reveals And What They Mean

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1514 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Slashfilm

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that the fresh "Avengers: Doomsday" trailer reveals MCU heroes assembling for their biggest battle yet.
  • The final "Doomsday" trailer doesn't actually feature any major reveals, which is a good thing for those who prefer to keep their theater experience as pure as possible.
  • The upcoming "Doomsday" trailer finally gives Cyclops the X-Men line fans were waiting for, when Marsden's hero delivers his "To me, my X-Men" rallying cry to assemble his mutants, the Avengers, Fantastic Four, and several other heroes.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that the fresh "Avengers: Doomsday" trailer reveals MCU heroes assembling for their biggest battle yet. It will also surely be one of their most profitable, given the hype around this movie. Despite Marvel Studios' well-publicized troubles of late, the Avengers' return remains highly anticipated. As such, any new revelations Marvel is willing to provide about the team-up movie are significant to say the least.

The final "Doomsday" trailer doesn't actually feature any major reveals, which is a good thing for those who prefer to keep their theater experience as pure as possible. For those who like to know as much as they can ahead of a Marvel Cinematic Universe release, however, it means much of the movie remains a mystery. (We're still no clearer on whether Robert Downey Jr.'s Doctor Doom is actually a Tony Stark variant or not, despite Marvel Studios head Kevin Feige's recent comments.) That said, the latest tease did contain several notable moments that have only served to increase the already significant hype.

The upcoming "Doomsday" trailer finally gives Cyclops the X-Men line fans were waiting for, when Marsden's hero delivers his "To me, my X-Men" rallying cry to assemble his mutants, the Avengers, Fantastic Four, and several other heroes. But beyond that tantalizing glimpse at the film's big showdown, there are several other notable moments, and lucky for you, we've gone and rounded 'em up.

In a recent development, the precise plot of "Avengers: Doomsday" remains under wraps for now, but at this point, we can pretty much piece together the major beats. Previously, co-director Joe Russo told Empire that Robert Downey Jr.'s Victor Von Doom is a "father who's a victim of trauma" and that he "lost a child." That lined up with what we've seen in previous trailers, wherein Vanessa Kirby's Sue Storm/Invisible Woman talked about how Doom "used to be different" before "everything he loved was taken from him." Now, the latest "Doomsday" trailer has confirmed that the Avengers themselves are responsible for it all.

In the latest trailer, Chris Evans' Steve Rogers can be heard saying, "Years ago, we did what was needed to make the world right," in reference to the events of 2019's "Avengers: Endgame." He continues: "But we didn't know those choices would have consequences." It seems that Steve's choice to travel back through time to be with his lover, Peggy Carter (Hayley Atwell) — and whatever the Avengers did to defeat Josh Brolin's Thanos — caused some sort of multiversal upheaval in which Doom's daughter met her, well, doom.

According to recent reports, this is why RDJ's villain tells the heroes of "Doomsday" that they've been living "stolen lives." With Steve's speech in the new trailer, it's all but certain he and the Avengers are responsible for whatever killed Doom's daughter, and likely the multiversal collapse referenced in the "Avengers Endgame: Encore" TVA scene. Turns out, Doom is the "consequence" to which Steve refers.

It has been revealed that thanks to what seemed like a hasty casting announcement prior to the final "Avengers: Doomsday" trailer, we knew Hailee Steinfeld's Kate Bishop would be appearing in the movie. Now, the trailer has given us our first look at the heir to the Hawkeye mantle in a very quick shot that demonstrates her looking up at something that's clearly got her very worried. But Kate might be just one of the Young Avengers to appear in the film.

It has been revealed that we know Scott Lang's (Paul Rudd) daughter, Cassie Lang (Kathryn Newton), is also part of "Doomsday." She demonstrates up briefly in the new trailer, too, looking as concerned as Kate. Interestingly enough, both characters are in their superhero suits, which suggests they'll be joining the big fight against Doctor Doom. That means two members of the Young Avengers will be involved in "Doomsday." Marvel Studios has yet to officially introduce these heroes as the superhero group from the comics, but has been slowly building up this new generation of Avengers over the past few years.

Recent findings suggest that the only likely member of the Young Avengers who hasn't appeared in trailers and is yet to be confirmed as being involved with "Doomsday" is Iman Vellani's Ms. Marvel. According to Andy Serkis, Ms. Marvel will appear in "Doomsday," but Marvel hasn't made that official. Otherwise, there are a handful of other young heroes that could show up and potentially form the Young Avengers proper in the movie itself, including Riri Williams/Ironheart (Dominique Thorne) and America Chavez (Xochitl Gomez). For now, it looks more likely than ever we'll see an official Young Avengers group unite in "Doomsday.".

It has been revealed that the newly introduced "Avengers: Doomsday" trailer shows Chris Hemsworth's Thor rising from the floor surrounded by yellow lightning as opposed to his typical blue lightning. That's significant, as it all but confirms he'll be wielding a powerful new force known as the Odinforce. This power, created by the Kings of Asgard, is a major upgrade for the character, and the latest trailer appears to have shown it in action.

According to recent reports, one of the most frequently showcased "Doomsday" scenes thus far has been the moment in which Thor launches himself at Doctor Doom, only to be stopped mid-air and flung backwards by the villain's formidable force (which, as it happens, involves a Jacky Kirby-inspired energy blast from Doom). Clearly, the God of Thunder is as outmatched as the rest of his cohorts.

Sources indicate that but back when the first four teaser trailers for "Doomsday" dropped, we saw Hemsworth's hero begging his father for the "strength of the All-Fathers." Since then we've seen concept art and a "Doomsday" billboard that seemingly spoiled the fact Thor was getting a major upgrade in the form of the Odinforce. It's this force that turns his lightning yellow, and the final "Doomsday" trailer is the first time we see footage of it in action. The brief shot shows Thor ascending in a forest, which looks to be the same forest in which he begged for the strength of the All-Fathers in the original teaser. Looks like he got his wish. Whether it will prove effective against Doom, however, remains to be seen.

It has been revealed that we got our first look at the X-Men in "Avengers: Doomsday" courtesy of the X-Men-heavy trailer back in January 2026. Since then, we've learned how the mutants might find their way to the Avengers. The film will take place during the collapse of the multiverse, whereby several "incursions" will see planets and timelines collide. These collisions are likely to be the reason for the film's major crossovers, i.e. the Fox-era X-Men and the Fantastic Four arriving on the Avengers' Earth 616. But it seems when the X-Men and Avengers first come face to face they initially clash, as evidenced by footage from prior trailers in which Yelena Belova/Black Widow (Florence Pugh) takes on Mystique (Rebecca Romijn) and Shang-Chi (Simu Liu) battles Gambit (Channing Tatum).

Now, however, the final "Doomsday" trailer has confirmed that Anthony Mackie's Sam Wilson/Captain America will face off against James Marsden's Scott Summers/Cyclops. The trailer demonstrates the pair going toe-to-toe in what looks to be a pretty brutal clash, with Wilson holding Cyclops by the neck as he unleashes an optic blast. Clearly, the X-Men and Avengers ultimately manage to, as Thor puts it, "put aside their petty squabbles." But for at least a moment, the two superhero teams will be at odds in the movie, and Sam Wilson's showdown with Scott Summers looks set to be a major highlight.

The final "Avengers: Doomsday" trailer reminds us of the main threat facing Earth 616 in the movie. While Doctor Doom is the substantial bad, the entire multiverse is collapsing, and in the latest trailer we see a brief shot that shows two planets in the sky above Fresh York City. The trailer also features several shots of heroes looking up at the sky, or out of windows and reacting with shock and dismay, and it's likely this planetary incursion is what has them so upset.

It has been revealed that we've known that the heroes of "Doomsday" would be dealing with multiversal collapse in the film for some time. But this is the first shot we've seen in an official trailer that shows planets on a collision course with Earth. Previously, a Dunkin' Donuts commercial gave us our best look at the threat the Avengers face in "Doomsday," with a shot showing a planet looming in the sky over Avengers Tower. But it looks as though multiple timelines/planets are set to collide with Earth based on the brief scene from this latest trailer.

Exactly which planets these are remains unclear. One may in fact be the Fox-era X-Men's world, and this cityscape view could be giving us a glimpse of their arrival in the Avengers' timeline. Either way, clearly the stakes have never been higher, as failure means the complete and utter destruction of the multiverse.

"Avengers: Doomsday" hits theaters on December 18, 2026.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, blade Runner 2099 has arguably been one of the most anticipated titles on the 2026 TV schedule, and there’s a good reason for that.
  • Sources indicate that if there’s anything to know about the Blade Runner universe, it’s that it has major dystopian vibes, and that particular aura is definitely present in 2099.
  • Recent findings suggest that blade Runner 2099 is a disappointing continuation of the iconic series which leans too heavily into the dark and downbeat side of its future dystopia rather than finding ways to elevate its lead characters in that world.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, blade Runner 2099 has arguably been one of the most anticipated titles on the 2026 TV schedule, and there’s a good reason for that. Not only does it expand upon the classic science-fiction franchise, but it also has two capable leads in Michelle Yeoh and Hunter Schafer (who do plenty of stunt work). The show debuts later this week, and reviews are finally starting to roll in. Having seen the show in its entirety for myself, I figured there would be high praise for the visuals, but I am surprised by one particular critique amongst critics.

Sources indicate that if there’s anything to know about the Blade Runner universe, it’s that it has major dystopian vibes, and that particular aura is definitely present in 2099. The series continues to highlight a version of Los Angeles in the distant future that’s far from pristine. Surprisingly enough, though, it seems that the show is proving to be a little too dark for some pundits’ liking. Scott Collura of IGN praises the visual style of the series, though he takes matter with just how bleak the proceedings get:.

Recent findings suggest that blade Runner 2099 is a disappointing continuation of the iconic series which leans too heavily into the dark and downbeat side of its future dystopia rather than finding ways to elevate its lead characters in that world. Michelle Yeoh and Hunter Schafer are both miscast as a buddy-cop team that subsist on fear and mistrust and angst, while the more interesting characters don’t get nearly enough to do. While the production design, visual effects and overall look of the show are a wonder to behold, 2099 also leans so heavily into its creators’ own fandom at times that it can be distracting.

According to recent reports, 2099 – which, of course, takes place 50 years after 2017’s Blade Runner 2049 – sees Replicants having become the ruling class, while humans are treated like vermin. At the center of the story is Cora (Hunter Schafer), a human trying to escape her circumstances by posing as a Replicant Blade Runner. In the process of doing that, she is partnered with Olwen (Yeoh), a dying Replicant Runner. The story does indeed get dark, but I didn’t have much of an issue with it. As for The Guardian’s Rhik Samadder, though, he indicates:.

Sources indicate that if you’re a cyberpunk who mainlines ennui and likes watching actors you can’t see, speaking words you can’t hear, this show may well knock your fishnet socks off. But why spend this much time immersed in a doomed world, when you could open up a window and watch the real one? It’s live!

According to recent reports, samadder also notably calls the visuals both “impressive” and “oppressive” in a way. However, also mentioning that the series also “plunges us into a far darker world” than the Blade Runner movies (which don’t directly tie into 2099). Likewise, Aaron Pruner of CNET isn’t really a fan of the overly dark setting and aesthetic. In his somewhat mixed review, Pruner praises the show’s execution while also posing this question regarding the bleak vibe:.

Could a little bit of levity help break up the monotony? Possibly. But, again, that would go against the grain of the Blade Runner franchise. And not for nothing, the original wasn’t at all funny, yet nuanced characters like Roy Batty (Rutger Hauer) and Pris (Daryl Hannah) brought life and color to the dreary, rain-slick streets of Ridley Scott’s original.

Sources indicate that the darkness doesn’t seem to be deterring everyone, though, as Alison Herman of Variety has glowing thoughts on the show. Aside from praising Hunter Schafer, Herman also admires series creator Silka Luisa’s adherence to this storied continuity birthed by Philip K. Dick:.

Recent findings suggest that ‘Blade Runner 2099’ dutifully incorporates the franchise’s visual and thematic touchstones. Despite the passage of time, computer screens still have the blocky, vintage look of early PCs; a psychotically violent replicant named Clotilde (Amy Lennox), an early convert to a cult of personality that promises her and Olwen’s kind eternal life, is a clear echo of Daryl Hannah’s cartwheeling Pris from the original film. ‘Blade Runner’ has always hewn to the beats of a detective noir, and over time, has acquired mainstays of its own that ‘2099’ dutifully nods to.

That’s definitely a big compliment, considering how beloved Ridley Scott’s original 1982 film is and how much critical praise Denis Villeneuve’s 2049 received. Still, not everyone is impressed. TVLine’s Dave Nemetz finds the sci-fi show to be overly bleak as well. Not only that, but he also isn’t too taken with the visuals like a number of others are:.

We get it: The L.A. of the future is a rough scene. But there's no spark of joy or hope here to offset the bleakness... just more bleakness. ‘2099’ should at least provide some sci-fi eye candy, but the visuals are a disappointing rehash of the sleek, neon-soaked aesthetic of the original ‘Blade Runner.’.

Although I can’t say I saw these critiques about the show’s vibe coming, I can’t blame others for not caring for its dark nature. To me, this kind of style is just baked into the DNA of the franchise, though I can admit that Blade Runner 2099 does delve into murkier territory at times. I’m curious as to how fans will feel when all eight episodes of the show become available for Prime Video subscription holders on November 25.

Latest Update: There's Actually a Simple Explanation for All These Widespread Outages
