Check out our GTA 6 beginner guide to get a grasp of the basics and our tips for what to do first, recommendations for the best ways to make money fast, and an explainer for how to keep stolen weapons and cars to make the most of your free time.

Our selection of GTA 6 guides includes help for things like how to steal the Phoenix in "Unwanted Attention" and whether you should defuse Mandy, too. There's a set of explainers for GTA 6's more open-ended side activities, like how to rob the Exotic Animal Front and where to find tree effigies for the Skunk Ape mission, and we've got all the GTA 6 cheat codes. You'll have to put in some effort before you can use those, though.

The Naruto Movie Sounds Like It Could Be Better Than We Ever Imagined

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that fresh off making the best "Spider-Man" movie in about a decade with "Brand Fresh Day," director Destin Daniel Cretton is plunging into the Land of Fire and ninjas, adapting Masashi Kishimoto's manga/worldwide phenomenon "Naruto" into a live-action film, two years after it was first unveiled.
  • Deadline has reported that actor Hiroyuki Sanada ("Shogun," "John Wick: Chapter 4") is in negotiations to star in "Naruto" as Hiruzen Sarutobi, the Third Hokage and leader of Naruto's ninja village, Konohagakure.
  • It has been revealed that this alone suggests "Naruto" is serious about getting impressive talent: one of the coolest actors alive in Sanada, and a major young actor in Melton, who's won acclaim for his performances in "May December" and "Beef" Season 2.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that fresh off making the best "Spider-Man" movie in about a decade with "Brand Fresh Day," director Destin Daniel Cretton is plunging into the Land of Fire and ninjas, adapting Masashi Kishimoto's manga/worldwide phenomenon "Naruto" into a live-action film, two years after it was first unveiled. Translating a battle shonen manga/anime into live-action carries negative associations of past, failed attempts. Why bother moving a story designed to stretch reality's limits to a medium that's inherently more confining than a hand-drawn one? Will "Naruto" break this curse? It has a huge stage to do so, and the early steps look promising.

Deadline has reported that actor Hiroyuki Sanada ("Shogun," "John Wick: Chapter 4") is in negotiations to star in "Naruto" as Hiruzen Sarutobi, the Third Hokage and leader of Naruto's ninja village, Konohagakure. Sanada is the second major actor rumored to be joining "Naruto," after reports in August that Charles Melton had been approached to play Kakashi Hatake, Naruto's masked sensei.

It has been revealed that this alone suggests "Naruto" is serious about getting impressive talent: one of the coolest actors alive in Sanada, and a major young actor in Melton, who's won acclaim for his performances in "May December" and "Beef" Season 2. Not for nothing, Sanada and Melton are Japanese and Korean American, respectively — no whitewashing here, so far, contrary to "Naruto" fans' long-standing jokes about Tom Holland or Timothée Chalamet starring as Naruto.

Industry observers note that "Naruto" has launched a "global" search/audition process for the movie's three young leads: Naruto and his teammates Sasuke Uchiha and Sakura Haruno. That suggests the film's creators are looking for young actors — possibly, even plausibly, unknowns — who can embody those characters first without prioritizing pre-existing star power.

Casting Hiroyuki Sanada as the Third Hokage suggests the "Naruto" team is already looking to the horizon and seeing sequels. Hiruzen is only a background part of the first "Naruto" arc, "The Land of Waves" (which is the ideal starting place for a movie series). But he takes center stage in the second and third arcs, where one of his former students, the snake-like Orochimaru, serves as the main villain. Hiruzen gets a major action sequence confronting Orochimaru, and casting Sanada — a martial artist who holds a black belt in karate, just as Charles Melton has one in taekwondo — seems like casting with that scene in mind.

If the goal is adapting the "Naruto" manga as a whole, then forward thinking will be key. The manga runs 700 chapters, divided into several story arcs; you'd likely need somewhere between seven and 10 movies to complete it. The live-action "Naruto" is being produced by studio Lionsgate in partnership with Sony. Lionsgate recently proved once more that "The Hunger Games" is a reliable hit for them with the success of "Sunrise on the Reaping." But it's never smart to put all your eggs in one basket. "Naruto" hits overlapping demographic appeal and even some similar story beats as "The Hunger Games" (like children becoming killers and the tragic horrors of war).

In a recent development, moreover, comic books have become the prime IP of Hollywood these past two decades, and yet manga outsells American comics many times over. Manga/anime is in the cultural mainstream for anyone younger than a young millennial, and the first studio to crack that could be sitting on a cultural gold mine. So, yeah, Lionsgate has a strong incentive to get "Naruto" right, and the talent it's recruiting suggests they understand that.

Sources indicate that even if Destin Daniel Cretton doesn't stick around for any of those potential "Naruto" sequels (I have to imagine Sony and Marvel Studios want him back for more "Spider-Man" movies), getting him as director for the first is another sign that Lionsgate is taking this seriously. Look at what he's directed, and consider how he's intent on casting actors with genuine martial arts bona fides for "Naruto," and it's clear why he's the man for the job.

Industry observers note that an essential part of "Naruto" is its fight choreography, which is more choreographed around hand-to-hand martial arts than most other battle shonen. Yes, the ninjas in "Naruto" use "jutsus," or magical/superpowered attacks powered by spiritual energy, or chakra. But the core of the series' fight scenes is mano-a-mano fights that lay on the brutality and raw emotion; that's especially true in Naruto and Sasuke's various duels.

The combat in "Naruto" likewise employs parkour acrobatics in the vein of wuxia. (In-universe, ninja learn to channel their chakra to balance on, climb, and run through trees.) Cretton directing "Shang-Chi," a wuxia-flavored Marvel movie, and Spider-Man, who webslings through Fresh York City like how Naruto and his ilk dash through forests, gives him the perfect experience to deliver the heightened-but-not-completely intensity of the action from the early "Naruto" arcs.

Cretton also has the perfect sensei to consult with in Masashi Kishimoto, who has endorsed Cretton as the perfect director for the project, the same way that "One Piece" creator Eiichiro Oda personally approved elements of Netflix's "One Piece" series. "One Piece" proved live-action shonen manga/anime can work in the TV format, and "Naruto" might be the project that proves it can be a blockbuster movie.

"Naruto" is currently in development.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • The world may not have been champing at the bit for another “Meet the Parents” sequel with quite the same enthusiasm that defined the hype for “GTA VI” (pretty close, tho!), but anyone who’s been itching for another crazaaaazy weekend between neurotic nurse Gaylord “Greg” Focker and his imperious ex-CIA father-in-law Jack Byrnes has had to wait even longer for their prayers to be answered.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The world may not have been champing at the bit for another “Meet the Parents” sequel with quite the same enthusiasm that defined the hype for “GTA VI” (pretty close, tho!), but anyone who’s been itching for another crazaaaazy weekend between neurotic nurse Gaylord “Greg” Focker and his imperious ex-CIA father-in-law Jack Byrnes has had to wait even longer for their prayers to be answered. Was it worth it?

It has been revealed that well, let’s do a quick comparison between two cultural phenomenons that I’m definitely not just lumping together in a desperate — some might say “heroic” — attempt to write an involving review lede for a movie that never makes even the slightest effort to earn your attention. Related Stories Jane Fonda on Documentary ‘Gaslit,’ Trump, and What the Democrats’ Midterm Victory Means for Climate Change Paul Thomas Anderson’s ‘Cameron Winter at Carnegie Hall’ Getting Nationwide Release in January.

In a recent development, ahem: On the one hand, it took 13 years for Rockstar Games to produce another numbered installment of their marquee franchise, during which time they leveraged cutting-edge technology and unprecedented financial resources in order to radically iterate upon a proven formula so that the organization’s Baudrillardian allegory of American pathos would map onto an era that has become too shattered for more coherent sense-making. On the other hand, it took 16 years for the combined power of Universal and Paramount (a Skydance Company) to will another “Focker” movie into existence, during which time someone realized that it might be kinda funny if Robert De Niro said the words “Jamba Juice.”.

Sources indicate that and in fairness, they weren’t wrong. A Robert De Niro character shouldn’t know what Jamba Juice is, let alone want to drink there! Not only that, but he correctly emphasizes the “JAM” of it all, the formal precision of which suggests that Jack — a red-blooded Boomer who’s recently become an exercise-obsessed vegan health nut — has developed a sincere degree of respect for the smoothie chain and its various blended offerings, even if it’s taken him 16 years to do so.

Given that John Hamburg’s “Focker In-Law” brings back so much of the franchise’s original cast almost three decades since they first played these roles, the film benefits from a Linklater-esque sense of temporal continuity that invites us to imagine the time between movies as a living space. Don’t be fooled by the gruel-thin story, the parade of self-amused callbacks, or the painfully contrived jokes that substitute for real emotion, this isn’t an opportunistic cash-grab meant to capitalize on our collective appetite for big screen comedies — it’s a family reunion.

It has been revealed that the expectations for a legacy sequel are much lower than they might be for the most expensive video game in history, especially in the context of a franchise that’s sustained by the idea that the surname “Focker” sounds almost indistinguishable from the word “fucker.” (Don’t be embarrassed if you hadn’t put that together before — it’s subtle, and film critics are professionally trained to identify such things). “GTA VI” had to revolutionize interactive entertainment in order to be considered a success. “Focker In-Law” just has to deliver more of the same. It does that over and over and over again; I don’t know about Jack’s nipples, but Greg (Ben Stiller) can certainly milk an old joke until it turns to dust in his hand.

Industry observers note that the cinematic equivalent of half-rotten Thanksgiving leftovers that you’d only eat in lieu of having any other food in the house, “Focker In-Law” might be an increasingly rare big-screen comedy, but it’s endowed with the “whatever”-level apathy of the worst straight-to-streaming junk. Depressingly, that feels like a systemic failure more than a creative one, as Hamburg is a very funny guy who directed several of the better comedies of this century’s pre-Netflix era (e.g. “Along Came Polly”), and he’s far from the only proven talent who gets wasted here.

The basic story — for which Hamburg shares credit with Austen Earl and, curiously, Ilana Glazer — offers a natural riff on the franchise’s initial premise: Greg might wear Radiohead t-shirts and sport facial skin tighter than any scene in the movie around him, but he’s now older than Jack was during the first movie, which means he and his wife Pam (Teri Polo, making the easiest money of her life) have aged into the “Parents” who are due to be “Meet”-ed when their son Henry (an overqualified Skyler Gisondo) brings his massive-eyed new girlfriend Olivia (Ariana Grande) to Jack’s 80th birthday celebration.

According to recent reports, the joke, and it’s not a bad one, is that Greg — a beta male bozo who’s desperate to make his children and their partners feel welcome — immediately bumps against his probable daughter-in-law, while Jack — a dominant and unyielding patriarch whose “Circle of Trust” is harder to crack than a captured enemy spy — cottons to her from the moment she gets to his house. It helps, of course, that Olivia is an ultra-rigid life coach and former hostage negotiator who shares Jack’s taste for military discipline, as well as his knowledge of different polygraph technologies. Why she’s drawn to a softboi like Greg’s son remains unclear, but the “Wicked”-like theatricality of Grande’s performance is farcical enough for such open questions to be their own reward (it makes sense that her character would be so emotive and intentional), and at the end of the day what matters is just that Greg has a reason to feel rejected all over again.

Industry observers note that he doesn’t take it well! In fact, he acts like a massive asshole about it to a degree that steers the movie away from cringe comedy comfort food and closer towards a character study about a malignant narcissist instead. Stiller is a maestro of self-involved unpleasantness (his work in “Greenberg” and “The Meyerowitz Stories” has never gotten the recognition it deserves), but that kind of toxicity is far more unpleasant in the context of a film that thinks it’s cute and/or easily redeemable.

In “Meet the Parents,” Greg got into all sorts of wacky trouble because he meant well and cared so much about seeming worthy of Jack’s daughter. In “Focker In-Law,” the hijinks stem from the fact that he’s a scheming monster who’s trying to sabotage his son’s relationship so that Henry might stay closer to home. The clean and simple fun of watching good intentions curdle into misunderstood chaos has been replaced by the dull ache of watching someone try to pass off diagnosable psychosis as the stuff of routine parental anxiety.

Alarm bells start ringing from the very first comic setpiece, in which a classic setup — Greg tries to cut the airplane bathroom line by sneaking from coach into first class — is almost completely undone by the logic gaps that have come to define the character. Why does he impulsively steal Olivia’s birth control out of her bag before he even knows who she is, and how is it possible that such an overbearing dad hasn’t even seen a picture of his son’s very serious newly introduced girlfriend? Such questions aren’t really worth answering, and Hamburg at least has the courtesy to distract us from them with a fly-by cameo by Cole Escola, but the vibe is all the way off by the time we even touch down in New Jersey for the main event, and nothing that happens there is remotely inspired enough to redeem the pervasive sense that no one can remember why “Meet the Parents” became a franchise in the first place.

Was it Owen Wilson’s amusingly oblivious performance as Pam’s charmed ex-fiancé, Kevin? There’s only one way to find out! Was it Jack’s penchant for lie-detector tests or his affinity for unlovable pets? Let’s give them both a shot and see what sticks. (I was amused by the German shepherd he trains in this film, who sets up a very good joke accusation that I don’t want to spoil here). Maybe it became a phenomenon because people crave manic setpieces that end in a plume of human ashes — we should run that back just in case. Anything to avoid the obvious and enduring coziness of a “home for the holidays” movie, which “Focker In-Law” inexplicably forfeits by setting its story at the height of summer.

The ballad of Gaylord Focker certainly didn’t become a thing because of Greg’s daughter and her long-term boyfriend, whose presence this movie struggles to accommodate despite the fact that Beanie Feldstein and Eduardo Franco are both eager to help liven things up. In fairness, why open the floor to potentially amusing new characters when you can spend half the film’s runtime agonizing over Greg’s uncomfortably demented attempts to steal the engagement ring that Henry wants to give to Olivia? Some opportunities are just too good to pass up, I suppose.

That “Focker In-Law” maintains any of its series’ long-faded charm can be attributed to De Niro, who sleepwalked through the previous two sequels but feels revived by Jack’s newfound looseness in this one. The actor delights in playing off Grande’s type-A eagerness, just as his character takes a muted pleasure in how much Olivia causes Greg to crash out. In a comedy as flat, stilted, and generic as this one, De Niro’s still-inimitable star power is almost enough to save the movie from its own reheated cynicism. “JAM-ba Juice.” They actually just go by “Jamba” now. The franchise’s juice is long, long gone.

Universal Pictures will release “Focker In-Law” in theaters on Wednesday, November 25.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that it’s hard to believe the entire Critical Role table for Campaign 4 hasn’t been together since the Convergence arc in June. Since then, the Soldiers, Seekers, and Schemers tables have remained separate. Or, more accurately, the Seekers and Schemers tables have remained separate.

Sources indicate that since Critical Role Campaign 4 episode 31, "Trick of the Light," Critters haven’t seen hide nor hair of everyone’s favorite orc Druid, Thaisha Lloy. Nor have they received any confirmation about when, exactly, Travis Willingham will return with a new character, after his Paladin, Teor Pridesire, met an unfortunate end in episode 30, "Here in the Dark.".

Sources indicate that luckily, the wait is finally over. Critical Role revealed on Nov. 23 that its eagerly anticipated Soldiers table, featuring Aabria Iyengar as Thaisha, will return on Dec. 3 and Dec. 10 for a two-part Soldiers table arc. And she won’t be alone.

When the three tables split off in June last year, it seemed that the Soldiers table would consist only of Thaisha. In an interview with Polygon, Iyengar confirmed she wasn't sure at the time whether Thaisha’s story would be told through cold openings or off-camera. Later, however, the Critical Role team decided to give the Soldiers table a mini-arc following Thaisha as she explored her future on the druidic path. But she would not be doing all of that on her own.

“We’ve got some amazing guests, Celia Rose Gooding and Abubakar Salim," Iyengar told Polygon. "Two people who I have admired for so long; it was so fun to finally sit down and play with them. And, of course, the return of Travis Willingham and his new PC.”.

According to recent reports, willingham has been absent from Critical Role’s Campaign 4 since his katari Paladin, Teor Pridesire, died in episode 30. Teor was killed inside House Tachonis’s Obrimus Manor during a truly heartbreaking moment for the fans and the cast.

Gooding and Salim have both guest-starred on Critical Role before: Gooding appeared in Exandria Unlimited: Divergence as the half-elf Rei’nia Saph, while Salim has played various roles, most recently the fungril Berserker Mercy in Age of Umbra: Sallowlands.

Though Iyengar couldn’t reveal what characters Willingham and the other guests would play in this two-episode arc, she told Polygon they were all “deeply connected and bound by a similar purpose.”.

“Dol-Runja is the seat of the orcs and the druids in Kahan. So it's key and interesting to see multiple facets of that.”.

Recent findings suggest that since June, the Seekers and Schemers tables have been dealing with assassination attempts at the theater, watery heists, and literal hell. When we last checked in, the Seekers table — with the help of several NPCs like fey pixie Clauny the Rose, talking dog Dame Morgaine, and scoundrel Pimley Morn — successfully rescued the daughters of their ally, Ulbid Morn.

On Dec. 3, Critters will reunite with Thaisha, who set off for the city of Dol-Rungja. There, she hopes to speak with the Druidic people and persuade them to abandon their neutrality and help fight back against the Sundered Houses.

Recent findings suggest that whether that will work out for Thaisha remains to be seen. The last time she encountered other druids, a few of them weren’t too pleased with her role in bringing the Necromancer Wizard, Occtis Tachonis (Alexander Ward), back to life as a Hollowed One. Given that she’ll have to answer for it to very key people, including her grandma, we expect the orc druid to be put through the proverbial wringer over the course of her two-episode arc.

In a recent development, aabria Iyengar, Travis Willingham, and guest stars Celia Rose Gooding and Abubakar Salim begin their Soldiers adventure on Dec. 3.

  • In a recent development, per Variety, in a 10-page civil claim filed in the Los Angeles Superior Court on November 20, Fuqua has now been accused of assault, battery, and intentional infliction of emotional distress.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Antoine Fuqua, the director of the 2026 box office hit Michael, has been accused of battery and assault.

In a recent development, having earned $1.028 billion worldwide, the Michael Jackson biopic is the fourth highest-grossing movie of 2026, only behind Spider-Man: Brand New Day ($2.523 billion), The Odyssey ($1.805 billion), Toy Story 5 ($1.149 billion), and ahead of The Super Mario Galaxy Movie ($1.012 billion). Michael broke numerous box office records as well, including becoming the first biopic to ever reach $1 billion globally.

In a recent development, per Variety, in a 10-page civil claim filed in the Los Angeles Superior Court on November 20, Fuqua has now been accused of assault, battery, and intentional infliction of emotional distress. He allegedly pulled a handgun on a Los Angeles bar manager and struck him in the head last February.

According to the civil claim, the assistant manager of the bar Good Times at Davey Wayne's, William Rosenthal, denied entry to Fuqua, his son, Brando, and his daughter, due to them being "visibly overly intoxicated." After Rosenthal was spat on by a member of the group, he told them they needed to leave the bar.

Rosenthal alleges that an hour after this occurred, Fuqua and those in his group were still standing in the line outside the bar. He was then approached by Fuqua, who accused Rosenthal of pepper-spraying his daughter. After the bar manager denied this accusation, the director allegedly "pulled out a handgun," "struck" him in the face, and uttered "a racial and anti-Semetic slur," along with "threatening to kill him.".

The complaint goes on to state that "as Plaintiff staggered back in pain, Defendant Brando Fuqua appeared and approached Plaintiff and forcefully swung a handgun at Plaintiff’s face. Defendants Antoine Fuqua and Brandon Fuqua then pointed their handguns at Plaintiff, placing him in imminent fear for his life, before fleeing down the street.".

As a result of the "serious physical and psychological injuries" that include a nose fracture, head injury, skin lacerations, post-traumatic stress disorder, along with severe emotional distress and severe scarring that have led to ongoing "great physical and mental pain and suffering," Rosenthal is seeking $50,000. The claim also states that the bar manager believes his injuries "will result in some permanent disability.".

Sources indicate that in terms of Fuqua's career, a Michael sequel has not been officially announced by Lionsgate yet, although the studio's Motion Picture Group Chair, Adam Fogelson, shared during an earnings call in August that "we are targeting a production start towards the end of this year or early next. I think that the end of calendar ’27 and the first half of calendar ’28 would be the current thought of roughly where the movie would go. We’re not ready to announce everything at the moment.".

Prior to this, the ending of Michael set up a sequel by leaving much of the pop star's life uncovered and concluding with the line "His Story Continues." Fuqua has also previously spoken about how he filmed parts of the movie that had to be cut, and that there is already footage that could be incorporated into a potential sequel.

In a recent development, when discussing sequel ideas for Michael with ScreenRant's Liam Crowley in April, around the time of the first movie's theatrical release, Jaafar Jackson, who plays the titular character, shared that he "absolutely" would be interested in playing the role again. The actor is the real-life nephew of Michael Jackson.

Recent findings suggest that outside the music biopic, Antoine Fuqua and Denzel Washington have collaborated on numerous movies, including Training Day, The Equalizer, 2016's The Magnificent Seven, The Equalizer 2, and The Equalizer 3. Among his other directing credits are Tears of the Sun, King Arthur, Shooter, Olympus Has Fallen, Southpaw, Emancipation, and an episode of Prime Video's The Terminal List.

Tech Report: UK court rules Apple can share the top secret order everyone already knew

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (769 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: 9to5mac

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The Investigatory Powers Tribunal – essentially a British court that deals with complaints about state surveillance – has ruled that Apple is allowed to reveal a secret order it received from the UK government.
  • Apple had already found a clever way to alert British customers to the classified order without breaking the law, but it can now confirm what we all already knew, and talk openly about the matter ….
  • Industry observers note that the story centers on Apple’s introduction of the Advanced Data Protection (ADP) privacy feature back in 2022.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Investigatory Powers Tribunal – essentially a British court that deals with complaints about state surveillance – has ruled that Apple is allowed to reveal a secret order it received from the UK government.

Apple had already found a clever way to alert British customers to the classified order without breaking the law, but it can now confirm what we all already knew, and talk openly about the matter ….

Industry observers note that the story centers on Apple’s introduction of the Advanced Data Protection (ADP) privacy feature back in 2022. This extended end-to-end encryption to almost all your iCloud data, meaning Apple has no access, and therefore cannot grant access to any government agencies who come knocking on its door.

It has been revealed that the feature is off by default because it means Apple cannot help you access any of your data if, for example, you forget your iCloud password. However, those who want to maximize the privacy of their iCloud account can enable it.

In 2025, the British government ordered Apple to create a backdoor to allow access by security services and law enforcement. Even worse, the order was issued under legislation that prohibits companies from revealing that they have received this demand.

It has been revealed that this would have meant that British customers who enabled ADP would think that their data was safe when in fact it wasn’t. As we’ve noted many times before, any backdoor created for use by the good guys is vulnerable to discovery and exploitation by the bad guys.

It would have been illegal for Apple to reveal that it had been instructed to compromise the privacy of customer data, but the manufacturer found a clever way to effectively communicate this without breaking the law. Apple revealed it was withdrawing ADP from the UK without explaining its reason.

According to recent reports, “Apple can no longer offer Advanced Data Protection (ADP) in the United Kingdom to fresh owners and current UK users will eventually need to disable this security feature. ADP protects iCloud data with end-to-end encryption, which means the data can only be decrypted by the user who owns it, and only on their trusted devices. We are gravely disappointed that the protections provided by ADP will not be available to our customers in the UK […] As we have remarked many times before, we have never built a backdoor or master key to any of our products or services and we never will.”.

Tell me you’ve been ordered to create a backdoor to ADP without telling me you’ve been ordered to create a backdoor to ADP ….

Industry observers note that at this point, it was an open secret. However, ridiculously, despite the fact that everyone in the security and privacy field knew about it and was talking about it, Apple was still not allowed to officially confirm it.

It has been revealed that the iPhone maker asked the Investigatory Powers Tribunal (IPT) to allow it to openly discuss the order, with privacy campaigners backing this call. The Financial Times reports that the court has now ruled in Apple’s favor.

Industry observers note that the UK government must admit that it issued a secret order to Apple to allow it access to encrypted customer data, a court has ruled […] The Home Office has “not established that it would be damaging to national security” to reveal that Apple had received a “technical capability notice” (TCN), the tribunal said. The ruling means that […] “much” of Apple and the non-profits’ legal challenge can now take place in open court.

One of the great ironies is that most people had never heard of ADP until the government effectively made it headline news in the tech press three years after it released – a classic example of the Streisand Effect.

According to recent reports, this ruling is a win both for transparency and commonsense. To be clear, the actual requirement for a backdoor remains in place, but this can now be challenged in open court.

He has never directed a Western, despite having openly longed to put his spin on the type of movies that turned one of his idols, John Ford, into a legend.

Well, the wait is over. Spielberg is developing an untitled film for Focus Features about two fugitives charting a course across the American West, and he’s assembled a crack team to help him. The ensemble will include Jessie Buckley, fresh off her Oscar win for “Hamnet,” Cillian Murphy, the Oscar-winning star of “Oppenheimer,” and Mark Rylance, a frequent Spielberg collaborator who won, you guessed it, an Oscar for “Bridge of Spies.” Related Stories ‘Focker In-Law’ Review: An Eager Ariana Grande Isn’t Enough to Save a Comedy Sequel That Can’t Remember What People Liked About This Franchise Jane Fonda on Documentary ‘Gaslit,’ Trump, and What the Democrats’ Midterm Victory Means for Climate Change.

Recent findings suggest that but there’s more to get cinephiles’ hearts racing! Paul Thomas Anderson, the Oscar-winning filmmaker behind “Boogie Nights,” “There Will Be Blood,” and “One Battle After Another,” is writing the script. It’s based on Kevin Barry’s novel, “The Heart in Winter.” Though Anderson usually directs his screenplays, he’s done script doctoring for Ridley Scott (“Napoleon”) and Martin Scorsese (“Killers of the Flower Moon” and the upcoming “What Happens at Night”). He also did some work on “Corky Romano” — hey, they can’t all be winners! So why not join Spielberg’s merry band?

Spielberg is still one of the all-time greats, but he could use a hit. “Disclosure Day,” which marked his return to summer movies, was a box office disappointment, and his most recent films, like “The Fabelmans” and “West Side Story,” struggled to connect with audiences despite earning excellent reviews. Maybe saddling up will be just what the movie gods ordered.

Kristie Macosko Krieger, Sara Murphy, Anderson, and Spielberg will produce the film, which is expected to hit theaters in 2028. Tim Headington, Neil Shah, Ryan Zacarias, and Ana Leocha will executive produce it.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Grand Theft Auto 6 is absolutely packed with Easter Eggs, and seeing as the game has only been out for a short amount of time as of this writing, we've likely only seen the tip of the iceberg so far. However, by far one of the weirdest and wildest random encounter in the game that I've come across is located in a random warehouse in Vice City.

In a recent development, if you're a diligent player, you likely noticed the shipping container full of sex dolls when searching for a car during the "Meet The Heders" mission in Chapter 3. Lucia opens up several containers during this quest, and one of them is packed with sex dolls, which is funny by itself, but many players likely aren't expecting this to go anywhere beyond this brief scene. However, players can actually find an entire backstory to these seemingly random sex dolls if they know where to look, and it's absolutely terrifying if you're thinking of checking it out.

For starters, players will only be able to enter the sex doll warehouse if they're playing as Jason at night, though you can have Lucia with you when walking by the location. The best time to check out the warehouse is actually after completing the first main mentor mission with Yago, as it's located just across the parking lot once the mission ends. However, you can find the warehouse again by looking for the giant pink pistol statue nearby. See the map locations below for exact coordinates:.

According to recent reports, the warehouse itself is underneath a sign for Vice Noveltease, a firm that has been foreclosed due to a product recall, as you'll learn when you go inside. You'll see a large pane of glowing pink windows and a half open garage door that Jason can duck under, though it will close behind you automatically when you enter and Lucia will not be able to come in.

Once inside, prepare for a real horror show as the sex dolls are more than malfunctioning and borderline possessed. You can interact with each of the sex dolls as you enter, either taunting or defusing the situation, but either way they will bug out eventually and collapse. As you progress through the warehouse, you'll be attacked by several more sex dolls, both male and female, and there's even one with penis hands that will pin you down, so be ready for that.

It has been revealed that aside from demented sex dolls, there's also a rare collectible card on the workbench in there, Chastity from the America's Next Top Hooker set. There's also a Zombix in the First Aid Kit on the wall you can grab, but otherwise you can head out the door in the back. You'll be attacked on your way out, and if Lucia is with you, she won't be able to shoot the sex dolls because you're in the way, and there will be some hilarious banter between the couple after Jason finally escapes.

You can check out our other GTA 6 guides here.

This is one of those incredibly weird and random encounters that make GTA 6 feel so alive and detailed, even if it is just a warehouse full of demented robot sex dolls.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that netflix has been the beneficiary of some surprisingly massive titles from other streaming services throughout 2026. A deal with Disney this fall landed them a small treasure trove of content to introduce to a newly introduced audience, including the first two seasons of Disney+'s hit Percy Jackson and the Olympians series, all four seasons of ABC's crime procedural Will Trent, and the entirety of the mainline Ice Age movies, to name a few. Each has since exploded on the platform to varying degrees during their limited stay, with the latter becoming perhaps the biggest winner of the bunch and completely taking over the top ten after their debut. However, their latest third-party acquisition from MGM+ is reaching some truly rare territory.

The first three seasons of the sci-fi horror mystery series From made its Netflix debut on October 19 after years of being one of the smaller streamer's hidden gems, and it immediately took off. Season 1 reached #1 on the platform's English television top ten for that week, marking the beginning of a dominant run that has yet to end. In every week since, all three seasons have charted somewhere in the top ten, proof of just how many viewers are getting lost in the Harold Perrineau-led series about a town that won't let anyone who enters its borders leave. Nielsen is now putting some numbers to the performance, with some shocking results.

In a recent development, for the week of November 2 through 8, From scored a staggering 1.685 billion minutes viewed, nearly doubling the next highest performer — Grey's Anatomy at 857 million — among all acquired series on streaming. No other series even got half as much viewership as the horror hit created by John Griffin and showrun by Jeff Pinkner. That's particularly notable considering there are only 30 episodes available to watch, whereas the next lowest on Nielsen's top ten, Bluey in fourth place, has 154 episodes available. It's extremely unique territory for a streaming acquisition of that kind, one that has now totaled over 5 billion minutes viewed since its arrival on Netflix.

Your nightmare is not really the doll. It is the face of the person you tell, and the way they decide, very kindly, that you have imagined all of it.

Your nightmare has your number, knows your name, and has almost certainly been inside your house before. The worst part is that you already know them.

Your nightmare is not really about you. It is about the people asleep down the hall, and the feeling that whatever is here is not interested in leaving.

The newfound Netflix interest in the residents of Fromville and the creatures that haunt them couldn't come at a better time, with MGM+ looking to bring the saga of survival horror to a close. Production began on the fifth and final season over the summer following a massive Season 4 cliffhanger that left the remaining survivors in a dire and deeply uncertain situation going forward. It'll mark the end of an era for the streamer, given that From was one of its biggest breakout darlings, earning rave reviews and comparisons to Perrineau's prior series, Lost, since its debut back in 2022. A premiere date hasn't been set for Season 5 just yet, but it's bound to bring back the main ensemble for one last scare, including Catalina Sandino Moreno, David Alpay, Elizabeth Saunders, Scott McCord, Ricky He, Hannah Cheramy, and Chloe Van Landschoot, among others.

From Seasons 1 through 3 are currently streaming on Netflix.

The 6 Most Outrageous GTA 6 Myths, Debunked

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1079 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Polygon

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • After a wild opening weekend, Grand Theft Auto 6 is off to the races.
  • It has been revealed that because of that, there are a lot of myths about GTA 6 at the moment floating around the internet.
  • The claim: GTA 6’s story forces you to do chores for Lucia instead of crimes.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

After a wild opening weekend, Grand Theft Auto 6 is off to the races. Millions are playing Rockstar’s enormous open-world game and discovering its complexities in real time. There’s a lot to unpack in a game that’s filled with intersecting gameplay systems across a long story, and some players are already taking advantage of that. At the same time, the opening days of GTA 6’s launch have been filled with misinformation, much of it fueled by culture warriors and content creators looking to turn outrage into clicks on social media platforms that incentivize such behavior.

It has been revealed that because of that, there are a lot of myths about GTA 6 at the moment floating around the internet. Some come from harmless misunderstandings, while others are more deliberate misrepresentations intended to scare off potential players. To help you navigate the noise, we’ve rounded up some of the most rampant myths currently circulating around GTA 6 and fact-checked them accordingly.

The claim: GTA 6’s story forces you to do chores for Lucia instead of crimes.

If you spent launch day watching reactions to GTA 6’s early hours roll in instead of playing, you might have walked away thinking that Rockstar made a chore simulator. That’s thanks to a few early missions that revolve around Jason getting his home ready for Lucia as she’s about to be released from prison. Players will paint a bedroom for her, fix a leaky roof, and repair some stairs. There’s also an optional quest where players can run errands to prepare for Lucia's arrival, like picking up groceries or buying her a necklace. All of this happens in the first few hours of the game. GTA 6 quickly ramps up after that, getting into the series’ usual flow of cop chases, heists, and shootouts. You can call it a slow start, but know that any mundane missions you’ve seen make up a very small amount of story that you’re likely to see in your very first play session.

The claim: GTA 6 doesn’t allow you to steal cars, or heavily restricts what you can steal.

While there’s a grain of truth to this, it has been heavily exaggerated on social media. There are some select cars that you can’t steal in GTA 6, like those around Jason’s neighborhood or in an NPC’s car lot. But for the most part, you can jack just about any vehicle you see in Leonida. The catch is that you’ll need a device that can copy keys to get into some of the more expensive cars, and you won’t get that until Chapter 3. Being able to steal anything requires some patience as you play through the story, but be rest assured that you can do as much grand theft auto as ever in Grand Theft Auto.

The claim: Airplanes will bounce off of buildings instead of exploding on impact.

It has been revealed that this one is a little tricky to unpack because there seem to be two weird things colliding here. After videos of airplanes bouncing off of skyscrapers like rubber began to emerge on social media, players deduced that content creators were sharing videos where they had their Reduced Vehicle Damage setting turned on. It seemed like a textbook case of outrage farming, though there may be a slight bit of truth here. Some players have speculated that GTA 6 may have a few physics bugs that make it tough for certain airliners to blow up as expected. That may be an edge case, but I can confirm that I have crashed plenty of planes into buildings in GTA 6, and they have all exploded into a fiery wreck so far.

The claim: GTA 6 features no autosave, and you will lose progress if you don’t manually save.

It has been revealed that when players started reporting that they were losing hours of gameplay because GTA 6 didn’t have an autosave feature, I was very confused. I can open my save file right now and see a dedicated auto save slot that is regularly refreshed as I play. I initially wrote it off as players either lying or not realizing that the auto save only triggers after completing major missions, but it turns out they weren’t hallucinating. GTA 6’s first patch fixed an concern where auto save wasn’t triggering properly. So, yes, GTA 6 does have autosave; it just wasn’t working correctly for some players at launch. It shouldn’t be a problem now, but always remember to save early and often just in case.

The claim: Lucia is cheating on Jason during the story.

This one is downright bizarre. One of the first talking points that came out about GTA 6 was that Jason is a “cuck” who does not realize that Lucia is cheating on him. As someone who has played through the story, I spent days trying to figure out where in the world that blatant lie could be coming from. It turns out it was a good old misinterpretation. Early in the story, Lucia sends a text to an unknown character, which she rushes to hide from Jason when he enters the scene. While some have interpreted that as Lucia having a secret lover, it actually turns out that she was texting a friend from prison. To players’ credit, the scene does feel like it’s built to make you think Lucia is hiding a major secret from Jason, so that reaction might have been exactly what Rockstar was hoping to provoke.

The claim: GTA 6 does not allow you to open fire and kill people in a gay club.

The ugliest rumor to come out of GTA 6 so far is that the game will not allow you to walk into a gay club in Vice City and kill people. There was even a clip going around social media that seemed to support that, sparking some grotesque reactions. The truth is that the location in the video isn’t specifically a gay club. It is a club, and it’s true that you can’t open fire in it, but that’s only because you can’t shoot inside any establishment in GTA 6. This claim would technically be true if there was a gay club in the game, but only as a side effect of the wider systems working the way they do. What is true, though, is that the game features an unkillable non-binary character, according to the actor who portrayed them.

It has been revealed that apple has three main Apple Watch "lines." There's the flagship, presently the Series 12, which represents Apple's mainstream wearable. For athletes and users who think they'll put their watches through some extreme scenarios, there's the Ultra line, currently the Apple Watch Ultra 4. And while both the Series 12 and Ultra 4 are excellent devices in their own right, they can be pretty pricey (particularly the Ultra). That's why the third category, the SE, is actually best for most people, and Lifehacker's choice for best smartwatch gift of the year. Better yet, the third-generation SE is currently $50 off ahead of Black Friday, perfect for most people asking for an Apple Watch this year.

In a recent development, the SE 3 does just about everything you'd expect an Apple Watch to do. It, of course, has a heart rate sensor to keep tabs on your pulse, including high and low heart rate alerts; the ability to track dozens of different workouts and exercise types (including swimming, thanks to the device's water resistance); a sleep tracker with daily analyses available in the Health app; notification forwarding to check in on your alerts without opening your iPhone; and the ability to send and receive text messages.

It comes in two sizes (40mm and 44mm) depending on how large or small you prefer your watch. No matter which model you get, the watch comes with the S10 chip, Apple's last-generation watch processor. While it isn't as fast as the current S11 chip, the S10 is more than capable of running watchOS 27. Apple indicates the SE 3 can run for up to 18 hours on a single charge, and up to 32 hours in Low Power Mode, with fast charging from 0% to 80% in 45 minutes.

According to recent reports, the majority of the features missing from the SE 3 aren't essential. Apple's other watches have things like bigger, brighter displays, additional health tracking tools like hypertension alerts and an ECG sensor, longer battery life, and Audio Intelligence—the latter of which might be a benefit to miss, depending on who you are.

If your giftee wants or needs any of those additional features, Series 12 or Ultra 4 might be a better choice. But for anyone who wants the essential Apple Watch experience, the SE 3 is simply the best-value watch Apple sells right now—especially at this discount. Right now, the watch starts at $199 for the 40mm watch, or $229 for the 44mm. You can also save on the cellular versions of these watches: $249 for the cellular 40mm watch, and $279 for the cellular 44mm model.

Sources indicate that yes, Apple participates in Black Friday, though you may want to compare their sales with other retailers like Best Buy and Walmart. So far, the best Black Friday sale on an Apple product is the M5 MacBook Air on sale for $200 off, the lowest price since the price hike this summer.

Sources indicate that black Friday sales officially begin Friday, Nov. 27, 2026, and run throughout “Cyber Week,” the five-day period that runs from Thanksgiving through Cyber Monday, Nov. 30, 2026. But Black Friday and Cyber Monday dates have expanded as retailers compete for customers. You can get the same Black Friday sales early, and we expect sales to wind down by Dec. 2, 2026.

Recent findings suggest that this feels weird to say for me after 40 years of being overwhelmingly picky, but I was a super picky eater. Saying "was" just doesn't feel right, but going to Gourmet and Golf actually helped me break out of my picky-eating habits.

Sure, it's only been a couple of weeks, and I have to keep the momentum going by continuing to try upcoming foods, but I feel confident saying I was a picky eater, not that I am one.

I tried shrimp, lobster and other foods I've had in the past and didn't like. I confirmed I still don't like them, but I tried them without hesitation.

Recent findings suggest that it was like a food blur, and just about everything I tried was great. I counted for the first couple of days of the trip, but eventually the whirlwind of new foods became too much. I'd guess I tried at least 40 new foods.

If you're a picky eater like me, Gourmet and Golf could change your approach to food if you let it. And if you're not a picky eater (like my girlfriend Andria, who accompanied me on the trip), then you're in for a treat, because the food is some of the best you can get. There's a reason these are Michelin-starred chefs — they know what they're doing.

Industry observers note that okay, so the food was good. It changed my life and helped me overcome my fear of trying newly introduced foods. Good for me, right? But how were the Nicklaus-designed Bahia and Pacifico golf courses?

I keep track of my golf course ratings on a cool app called Eden. In it, Winged Foot West is my number one course — it gets 10 on my rating scale. Now, though, it has another course nipping at its heels, with the Pacifico course at Punta Mita getting a 9.9. And it's close — while ranking the courses, I actually considered putting Punta Mita above Winged Foot West based primarily on the blend of incredible vistas and the overall quality of the golf.

In the end, the history and legacy offered by Winged Foot gave it a slight edge, but it's close. And the Bahia course isn't far behind, coming in as the 7th best course I've ever played (beaten by Winged Foot West, Tamarack Country Club, Pacifico, Country Club of Waterbury, Scottsdale National and PGA National). Between the two courses, Punta Mita is clearly a destination with golfers in mind.

Punta Mita's golf courses come with some serious pedigree, and they live up to the challenge for which Nicklaus is known.

Which would explain why I shot a 115 during the best ball portion of the tournament.

These are hard golf courses designed to test every aspect of your golf game with massive, intelligently placed bunkers, narrow fairways, undulating greens, false fronts and all the other tricks that rack up strokes.

But nothing about the design feels haphazard or just there to make things difficult. It's all built to reward smart course management and good shots — something I was apparently incapable of during this particular trip (to give you some perspective, I typically shoot in the mid-to-upper 90s, so I shot almost 20 strokes more than normal).

Industry observers note that you know what? I don't care. My partner didn't care. It's hard to care what you shoot when you're surrounded by such beautiful scenery, like you are on both the Bahia and Pacifico courses at Punta Mita. And when the round was over, I knew I had some of the best culinary delights I've ever experienced waiting for me (and strategically placed around the two courses).

In a recent development, it doesn't matter what you shoot; you will have a good time at Gourmet and Golf. Just ask my partner — she didn't even play golf and can't stop talking about going back for another year.

  • Microsoft is saying goodbye to its task management service To Do, including the Mac and iOS apps.
  • The last day to use the To Do apps is June 30, 2027.
  • “Microsoft To Do is retiring,” Microsoft explains.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Microsoft is saying goodbye to its task management service To Do, including the Mac and iOS apps. Here’s what users need to know.

The last day to use the To Do apps is June 30, 2027. That date also applies to Windows, Android, and the web. The underlying service and sync support will retire later, according to Microsoft’s support document.

“Microsoft To Do is retiring,” Microsoft explains. “For work or school accounts, Microsoft Planner will be the destination for managing personal work tasks alongside assigned work. The updated My tasks experience begins rolling out in December 2026.”.

According to recent reports, on the Mac, you can use Planner on the web or in Teams. Microsoft explicitly says it has no plans for a native Mac app.

You can still see your existing To Do tasks in Planner through June 30, but your tasks and lists won’t carry over. Microsoft plans to offer an export option before the apps retire.

Planner doesn’t support personal Microsoft accounts however. If that’s how you use To Do, you’ll need to pick another task manager, even if you pay for Microsoft 365 Personal or Family, according to the company.

It has been revealed that the June shutdown will end a run of just over a decade for To Do on Apple platforms. Microsoft bought the tech giant behind Wunderlist in 2015 and released the first iPhone preview of To Do in April 2017.

Looking for a proper replacement? Apple’s built-in Reminders app can keep lists in sync between Apple devices, including a grocery list you share with family through iCloud.

Microsoft has been trying to make Teams as the super app for some time now, as Planner is integrated into Teams. Teams is one of the prime examples of why super apps are terrible, with a bloated, web app-like experience.

If you liked To Do because it worked across platforms, Todoist has apps for iPhone, iPad, Mac, Windows, and Android.

Sources indicate that does this sunsetting affect you? Were you a Wunderlist user back in the day? Share your thoughts in the comments.

Update: Howard Crow, Director of Product, Agents and AI, Microsoft, shared this statement with 9to5Mac regarding the transition:.

“We’re bringing task management experiences together across Microsoft 365 to make it easier for customers to manage individual tasks and team aims. As part of this transition, Microsoft To Do apps will retire on June 30, 2027, with work and school experiences coming together in Microsoft Planner. Existing integrations across Microsoft 365, including Outlook and Teams, will also be updated to work with Planner. We recognize this change will affect customers differently, particularly those using personal Microsoft accounts, and we’re committed to helping them prepare. Customers will be able to export their To Do data before retirement, and we’ll share additional guidance to support the transition.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that it's still a debate whether Grand Theft Auto 6 has the best gaming soundtrack of 2026, but it certainly has the most soundtrack of 2026. Rockstar Games' latest open-world crime epic features more than 800 songs, most of which you'll hear on its 26 genre-themed radio stations. Of all this breadth of wild music, you'd figure the most popular song on the soundtrack would be something that had overlap with a Fast and Furious OST. But it turns out the single best song in the GTA 6 soundtrack is something by... Nickelback?

Thanks to GTA 6, Nickelback's 2001 angst ballad "How You Remind Me" has been getting a lot of play — kind of. Technically, this version is a cover. GTA 6's Kaleidoscope FM radio station plays alternate-language versions of popular songs, the indisputable best of which is "Ola Afta Poui Fovamai," by the Greek singer and alternate former tourism minister Alkistis Protopsalti. As far as covers go, this is one for the ages. Seriously, listen:.

Industry observers note that you might be somewhat surprised to hear "How You Remind Me" making the rounds again, years removed from its days reigning over the Billboard charts. To this day, the most-played radio song of the 2000s has been relegated to background music in the daddest bars from Mississauga to Massapequa. It is arguably the epitome not just of Dad Rock but specifically of Divorced Dad Rock. If "How You Remind Me" was a person, its kitchen would include Slim Jims (assorted flavors), cold pizza (definitely pepperoni), and nothing else. It would drive a 2014 Corvette Stingray (bright red, obviously). It would live on the golf course.

But with "Ola Afta Poui Fovamai," Protopsalti injects a youthful, upbeat verve to Chad Kroeger's genius composition that legendarily emerged, nearly fully formed, from his brain in just 45 minutes following an argument with a partner. It's the sort of track you'd play in a convertible on a sunny day, or in the bathroom while getting ready for a party themed after The Devil Wears Prada (the good one). There is practically zero Divorced Dad energy in "Ola Afta Poui Fovamai." It is transformational.

I am far from the only person to completely lose my shit over the resurfacing of a song that hit number-one on charts in Austria, Canada, Denmark, Ireland, and the United Kingdom, in addition to peaking in the top ten in various other international markets. As of this writing, searches for "Nickelback" on Bluesky are all about "Ola Afta Poui Fovamai." On Facebook, Greek culture accounts are sharing the cover as a point of national pride. When Canadian streamer Dan "Greenskull" Hammill heard it for the first time in-game, he burst into a karaoke rendition that has since gone semi-viral.

Truth told, the Canadian rock quartet legitimately is one of my guilty pleasures. As a teenager, I once suffered a pretty serious concussion in a skiing accident; according to the paramedics, I spent the entire ride to the hospital singing "Photograph" in my unconscious state. Mortifying, but also hard to deny. Such is the allure of GTA 6. In being a mirror of our world, it's also a mirror of our lives, thus revealing truths we may not have otherwise been ready to admit. The boyfriends of the world start doing more chores for their partners. Those of us who've let the gym routine fall by the wayside pick it back up again. Nickelback? A guilty pleasure? I no longer see anything to be guilty about here.

  • Yamazaki’s sequel has already enjoyed a historic theatrical run of its own.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that hannah covers horror, sci-fi, and games at Collider, where she writes news and features, reviews upcoming releases, and interviews the people who make them. She’s helping build out Collider’s gaming coverage, with Pokémon as one of her specialties. If she isn’t writing about a monster, she’s probably watching one on a tape from her VHS collection.

Sources indicate that seventy-two years after Godzilla first emerged from the waters off the coast of Odo Island, Takashi Yamazaki has given the King of the Monsters two of his most celebrated movies. The Oscar-winning filmmaker has a tremendous appreciation for Ishirō Honda’s 1954 original, something that became especially apparent when he revisited Godzilla Minus One for its black-and-white theatrical release in 2024. Seeing Godzilla emerge from Tokyo Bay in monochrome was about as close as modern audiences could get to experiencing the monster the way Japanese moviegoers did seven decades earlier.

Yamazaki’s sequel has already enjoyed a historic theatrical run of its own. Godzilla Minus Zero opened to $30.6 million domestically, setting a record for a live-action foreign-language movie in North America. With its worldwide box office now estimated at over $110 million, the sequel is getting another opportunity to bring Godzilla fans back to theaters before the Christmas blockbuster season gets underway.

Recent findings suggest that according to a Regal listing, Godzilla Minus Zero/Minus Color is scheduled for a theatrical release on Friday, December 11. The black-and-white edition is listed with the same two-hour-and-15-minute runtime as the original, with Japanese audio and subtitles. Toho and GKIDS have yet to formally announce the release or confirm how long the alternate version will be playing in theaters.

According to recent reports, four franchises, four completely different ways of getting underneath your skin. This is the one built out of your particular fear, why it works so well on you, and what it would leave behind.

Recent findings suggest that your nightmare does not wait outside the door. It waits for you to close your eyes, which you are going to have to do eventually, because nobody has ever won that particular argument.

Industry observers note that your nightmare is not really the doll. It is the face of the person you tell, and the way they decide, very kindly, that you have imagined all of it.

Your nightmare has your number, knows your name, and has almost certainly been inside your house before. The worst part is that you already know them.

Your nightmare is not really about you. It is about the people asleep down the hall, and the feeling that whatever is here is not interested in leaving.

According to recent reports, when Yamazaki worked on Godzilla Minus One/Minus Color, he and his colorist individually adjusted the contrast of different elements within each shot. Turning the movie monochrome required making new creative decisions about everything from the visibility of Godzilla’s scales to the lighting on the actors’ faces. Yamazaki previously described the resulting version as “way scarier” than its color counterpart. It'll be interesting to see how that same approach affects Minus Zero, especially given the considerably larger scale of its kaiju encounters. Yamazaki’s sequel already draws heavily from the franchise’s Showa-era history, and seeing his latest monsters rendered in black and white should be an absolute treat for longtime Godzilla fans.

Sources indicate that the December 11 release also gives the sequel a week's head start before Avengers: Doomsday and Dune: Part Three open on December 18. For anyone who missed the original monochrome theatrical run of Minus One, which lasted just one week in January 2024, this is another opportunity to experience Yamazaki’s Godzilla on the big screen in a format that pays homage to the franchise's beginnings.

Godzilla Minus Zero/Minus Color is scheduled to hit theaters December 11.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • According to recent reports, it is a harsh reality of rewatching Game of Thrones that the groundbreaking series has aged terribly.
  • According to recent reports, game of Thrones' infamously rushed ending destroyed the character development that had been masterfully built over the first few seasons, and the intense multilayered political scheming gave way to sexual brutality and violence that became the norm rather than the game-changing exception.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that faith Roswell is a Senior Writer on Screen Rant's Classic TV team. Since earning her degree in Creative Writing over a decade ago, Faith has written articles on film and TV from a variety of different angles. Faith now combines her knowledge of psychology with her love of monster movies to give more insight into what makes the best ones. You may have read her Screen Rant lists and features covering horror, sci-fi, and fantasy, or read her Amazon Top 10 book, "Movie Monsters of the Deep." Faith has had an extensive career as a writer, appearing on BBC live radio, researching true crime for Rotten Mango podcast, and writing for publications including Mental Floss, Atlas Obscura, and The Daily Jaws before beginning here at Screen Rant.

According to recent reports, it is a harsh reality of rewatching Game of Thrones that the groundbreaking series has aged terribly. The series changed the way we approach fantasy TV by proving that far from being whimsical and child-focused, the genre could be as gritty and intense as any gangster show, while its enormous budget brought dragons and battles to life in a way rarely seen outside of blockbuster movies. Even so, while Game of Thrones remains one of fantasy TV's best epics, it has been overshadowed by the factors that turned its original fans off.

According to recent reports, game of Thrones' infamously rushed ending destroyed the character development that had been masterfully built over the first few seasons, and the intense multilayered political scheming gave way to sexual brutality and violence that became the norm rather than the game-changing exception. Now, many high fantasy TV shows are surpassing Game of Thrones, while fantasy of all subgenres are aging better, with many much older series overshadowing Game of Thrones and newer ones learning from its mistakes.

According to recent reports, like Game of Thrones, His Dark Materials is based on one of the greatest fantasy book series ever written, but the BBC's three-season fantasy masterpiece has an advantage over the longer show, in that the source material was a finished trilogy. Game of Thrones ran into problems when the TV series started to overtake George R. R. Martin's books, while Philip Pullman's books provided a clear framework for the way the story could be told onscreen.

Recent findings suggest that game of Thrones' early seasons had some flashes of wisdom that remain some of the best fantasy TV lines of all time, but the action and spectacle began to outshine the script, losing the show's best features. Instead, the series became known for sexual violence and dragons rather than infinitely quotable lines and political maneuvering. On the other hand, His Dark Materials never lost sight of its message warning viewers about the dangers of religious dogma and suppression, keeping it both timeless and just as interesting on a rewatch.

In a recent development, game of Thrones occasionally paid fan service, but The Magicians treated communication with its audience in a wildly different way, which is virtually guaranteed to give the series longevity. The show has been compared to Harry Potter for grownups, and its writers ensured this was addressed by making hilarious references to the controversial series. This cultural reference might have dated the show, if not for the fact that the characters are also heavy readers whose commentary on the fantasy genre is timeless, with many fantasy staples still being used to this day, including in Game of Thrones.

The Magicians also changed the fantasy genre, but in a more subtle way. Game of Thrones indicated what could be done with an enormous budget, but The Magicians addressed the psychological part of magic that few shows included. Rather than presenting magic as the solution to a problem, the series took a far more realistic approach, with mental illness, anxiety, and depression not disappearing with the right incantation. This approach is sometimes addressed in modern fantasy, but it is central to The Magicians, making the series feel both authentic and comforting.

Recent findings suggest that by the time Game of Thrones ended, viewers had largely stopped caring about the characters, even Jon Snow and Arya, whose further adventures once looked set to be perfect spinoff material. This dissatisfaction left viewers with little else to discuss, resulting in a franchise that is now being kept alive by its superior spinoffs and excellent source material. In contrast, Over the Garden Wall might only have lasted for ten minutes, but it is still one of fantasy's most intriguing series as it ended its perfect run with unanswered questions.

Following the adventures of two brothers navigating a mysterious forest, Over the Garden Wall's story and true meaning are still debated, with its themes resonating on different levels with viewers of all ages. That instantly makes it endlessly rewatchable, with a whimsical dark fantasy art style that will not age, while it feels inevitable that modern special effects will. Over the Garden Wall's total runtime is just under two hours, forever making it a much easier commitment than a multiple-season show with a disappointing ending.

Arcane is a perfect example of a genre-bending fantasy that creates something entirely upcoming while still fitting perfectly into the fantasy genre. Based on the League of Legends video game franchise, but telling an original story, Arcane straddles sci-fi, steampunk, and high fantasy without wasting a second of its runtime. Many fantasy TV shows are better than Game of Thrones, but Arcane outpaces it in virtually every way possible.

Both seasons of Arcane have a 100% positive critics' rating on Rotten Tomatoes.

According to recent reports, the multi-award-winning two-part series built a world that felt real and tangible, never lost its grip on its character development, and introduced a soundtrack that was the perfect finishing touch, outshining most other great fantasy TV series. Game of Thrones became too big for itself, neglecting the subtlety that defined its early seasons and dividing its characters along typical hero and villain lines, while Arcane is a masterclass in writing antiheroes.

Pushing Daisies is a fantasy TV show that was canceled before its time, making it into a forgotten gem that deserved more than its two seasons. This has allowed the show to age well, as fans are still invested in the fates of the characters, who deserve a fairytale ending, perhaps more than many Game of Thrones characters. The show, starring Anna Friel and a pre-Hobbit trilogy Lee Pace, centers on Ned (Pace,) a baker with the skill to bring the dead back to life with one touch, but kill them again with a second.

Recent findings suggest that this unique plot sets Pushing Daisies apart from virtually every other fantasy, including Game of Thrones, which is still a stereotypical entry for the genre, with its dragons and royals within a medieval-inspired setting. Pushing Daisies' central tragedy, with Ned being unable to touch his reanimated true love, has been turned into a bittersweet comedy, and with no subsequent show that comes close to improving on its tone, it is likely to continue aging like fine wine.

Sources indicate that avatar: The Last Airbender has a lot in common with Game of Thrones. Both series are high fantasy, featuring magic and warring nations, with warlords, quests, different cultures, and redemption arcs. However, Game of Thrones was heavily criticized for its regular sexual assault scenes and violence against women that many saw as gratuitous and unimaginative, neglecting the many other ways to drive a plot forward.

Recent findings suggest that despite being suitable for viewers of most ages, Avatar: The Last Airbender is sometimes gritty and emotionally heavy, but it does not include the graphic and sexualized violence that becomes a recurring theme in Game of Thrones. This alone has allowed it to age so well that many people who watched the series as children are now showing it to their own children. Avatar: The Last Airbender's best episodes are mini-masterpieces on their own, all combining to make a series with a consistent tone and lasting appeal, including on a rewatch.

Characters in Game of Thrones and Adventure Time grow up onscreen, and the tone of both shows shift, but while Finn's story sees him deal with complex emotions that bring more layers to the story, the coming of age of characters in Game of Thrones tends to be centered on marriage and sexual exploitation. Adventure Time might have been aimed at children, but it becomes more emotionally rich and layered over time than Game of Thrones.

Adventure Time was nominated for 16 Emmy Awards, winning eight of them.

It has been revealed that set in the land of Ooo, the surreal and imaginative Adventure Time grows with its audience, building on its own lore through Jake and Finn's adventures. Ooo has a rich history of its own, with past tragedies and surprising backstories for even its biggest villains, and one standout factor that beats even Game of Thrones fan favorite characters. Adventure Time's best characters are multifaceted, with few conforming to one archetype, like Princess Bubblegum, who is a ruler and scientific genius, while Game of Thrones often stuck with standard fantasy types, like warriors, queens, and adventurers.

Not all aspects of Buffy the Vampire Slayer have aged well. The series might be one of the best 1990s fantasy TV demonstrates ever made, but it is still a product of its time, and there was a long way to go for the portrayal of same-sex relationships onscreen. That mentioned, Buffy the Vampire Slayer paved the way for other TV shows to build on the good work it started, and it was revolutionary at the time it aired. Episodes like "Hush" played with format and this creativity made the show into a legend.

Like Buffy the Vampire Slayer, Game of Thrones began as a boundary-pushing TV show, but it did not take its initial pioneering approach much further. Characters like Brienne of Tarth were the exception rather than the norm, while Buffy the Vampire Slayer normalized women saving themselves and the world, and this has allowed the show to age better than most other fantasy TV series despite not being perfect itself.

There’s a new setting in iPadOS 27.3 that I instantly turned on and have been loving. It lets you double-tap the top of a window to resize it.

Inside Settings ⇾ Multitasking & Gestures, if ‘Windowed Apps’ is enabled there’s now a latest toggle: ‘Double-tap Top of Window to Zoom.’.

I’ve been using this gesture all the time in the beta, because it lets me resize my window to fullscreen then revert it to its previous size with ease. It’s an intuitive, convenient way to resize windows for different tasks.

Visual intelligence was available on iPad already, but iPadOS 27.3 adds a dedicated hub for using the feature: a newly introduced Siri mode in the Camera app.

It has been revealed that iOS 27 brought Siri mode to the iPhone’s Camera app, but it was missing from iPad. iPadOS 27.3 corrects that oversight, letting you use your iPad’s built-in Camera app to ask Siri about any object you capture.

Baking visual intelligence into Camera should expose the feature to a lot more iPad users, since before you had to set up a custom control or shortcut for it. And with how much better visual intelligence has gotten thanks to Siri AI, the Siri mode is a valuable addition.

Read more: iOS 27 gives the Camera app on iPhone a brand latest mode.

Freeform is gaining a variety of newly introduced features in iPadOS 27.3. They’re available in macOS and iOS too, but out of all Apple platforms, Freeform feels very much built for the iPad.
