📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Don’t let the title fool you: “The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth” might offer up a breezy, very fun-to-watch newly introduced entry into the life and times of titular (and fictitious) Hollywood stuntman, but co-star Elizabeth Debicki steals the show in David Fincher’s film (in addition to stealing the heart of Brad Pitt’s Cliff). Is it time to greenlight “The New Adventures of Karen Crosby”? We think so.

The much-anticipated sequel to Quentin Tarantino’s “Once Upon in Hollywood” picks up nearly a decade after the Oscar-winning antics of the previous film, finding Cliff pursuing newly introduced professional endeavors (film projecting! bartending! contract killing, kind of!). Stunt work? Eh, only when he feels like, and he certainly feels like after taking an unexpected meeting with Hollywood agent Karen Crosby (Debicki), whose grace and good humor instantly delight both Cliff and the audience. Related Stories Shawn Levy and 21 Laps Set Overall Film Deal at Sony Pictures Steven Spielberg Directing His First Western with Paul Thomas Anderson Writing the Script.

It has been revealed that tossed together by the wacky demands of Karen’s marquee client, actor Charlie Nelson (Scott Caan), the shaggy, Tarantino-penned “Cliff Booth” meanders its way through every corner of Hollywood, finding real emotional ballast and crackling chemistry every time Pitt and Debicki share the screen. Characteristically wordy and dense, we learn plenty about Karen along the way (including her early forays into film criticism and her current feelings about movies), and she wins Cliff’s heart by, well, literally and physically slapping the crap out of him.

Ahead, IndieWire catches up with the Aussie star (who gets to use her real accent this time) about Fincher’s film, from slapping her co-star to some serious ruminations on the instantly iconic “pig monologue speech.” No wonder Cliff went so crazy for Karen; she’s a delight.

The following interview has been edited and condensed for clarity and length.

IndieWire: What was your relationship with “Once Upon a Time in Hollywood” when the film came out in 2019?

According to recent reports, elizabeth Debicki: I went to see it in the cinema. I think I went by myself, which makes me think I must have been on a job. I was definitely in the States, maybe I was in L.A., and I went one afternoon. I went and sat in the cinema, and I loved it. It’s really vivid in my memory.

Recent findings suggest that I didn’t watch it again before we made this for performance reasons. In a way, I realized I didn’t really need to because, [there’s] something about Quentin’s movies, they just kind of wedge themselves in your brain. I can literally see the Playboy Mansion scene. I can see the Manson kids driving up to the house. I can see Margaret Qualley’s feet on the dashboard. I can see everything.

So it sounds like you came into this as a Tarantino fan.

Sources indicate that absolutely. Yeah. I mean, he’s seminal.

And to get Tarantino and Fincher is this incredible two-for-one.

It’s funny, because obviously in the making of this, I had to sort of normalize that. And they helped me do that because they were, from the second I got onto set — which was a two-week rehearsal period where we really worked through the script — we had Quentin for that whole period. [It was] very, very collaborative.

Industry observers note that A part of me wonders whether it was that thing where they have sat with the material for so long and had their full body relationship to it, and then I was fresh. I had my own thoughts and feelings. My memories of those rehearsal periods were really all three of them [Fincher, Tarantino, and Pitt] just turning to me and saying, “What do you think? What do you think?” The first time it happened, I was like, “Oh my God, what do I think?” After a little while, I started to actually say what I thought, which was great.

What was your audition process like?

According to recent reports, I didn’t audition for this. David emailed me and asked me if I would be interested in playing a part. I remember he phrased it in an email as he hoped that I would consider playing a very tricky part in a film he was hoping to make in July. It was a very David-ism kind of email. I think it said something like, “I hope you understand the seriousness of this conundrum,” or something. And I called him up and yeah, I was obviously ready to say, “I’ll do it.”.

He was very, very insistent. He was like, “Wait, wait, wait. I really want to tell you everything about it.” Because at that point he and Quentin were doing a massive edit of the script. He couldn’t send it to me there and then.

Karen is so singular, but she is in a familiar position if you’re working in Hollywood. Did you base any part of your performance on any agents or managers or publicists that you know or have encountered?

Recent findings suggest that when I first read the script, there were things that just rang so true to me, and might seem outrageous for anyone or slightly absurd maybe for anyone who doesn’t work in this industry. The incredible pig scene where Cliff talks about killing a pig, and then the scene in the car where Karen notes, “Now because of you, I now have to spend my entire morning finding a pig. That is not a joke, that is literally what I have to get up and do. And you know what? I had a lot of things I had to do, and it wasn’t find a pig. And now I have to drive your ass all the way to Marina del Rey because I have to just deliver you because that’s what my client needed.”.

According to recent reports, it’s kind of this absurd ask, but it’s folded into “that’s what I need for my process.” Quentin and David, they’re so fascinating because they are Hollywood. They are Hollywood, and also they sit outside it, and they observe it from these very, very unique vantage points. Quentin, in particular, his love affair with L.A. is so profound, and with Hollywood. Part of the thing I loved about her too is that she’s sort of accidentally an agent, which is not frequently do you come across that. One of the things too that feels very human about her is that she sort of had this other dream, but she took one really bad knock, and it broke her heart, and she just buried it deep inside and then made decisions based off that.

When we get to that scene with Karen and Cliff when you’re talking about how Karen had this other career as a film critic, I how much of that was lifted from what would’ve been Quentin’s movie, “The Movie Critic”?

I don’t know. I don’t actually know the answer to that question in terms of the parallel there. But I do love that in the middle of this film about 1977 in Hollywood, that there’s a really notable moment where we think about Pauline Kael, and we think about her and she lives in this film. I’m so glad that there’s this moment where my character gets to say, “Pauline Kael is my god,” because she was. She was incredible.

Industry observers note that as Karen, you have this great monologue explaining to Cliff who you used to be, what had happened with that career path, how wonderful it was that Pauline supported you, and then it didn’t work out. And then you have another monologue about seeing movies as hamburgers. It’s a really funny tension for Karen, because the audience likely assumes she loves movies and does see them as art.

That’s right, there is a tension there. I feel like one of the things that Quentin can do so well, and kind of totally unique to his own brain, is that he sort of plucks an idea out of the zeitgeist, something that we’re all thinking about, and he feeds it through his characters in a way that feels very organic. This is a big conversation that people are having as the industry shifts and changes. It also was a huge conversation that was happening in 1977. There was this big question of, “Is that art still if it’s commercial, if its box office success equates to this?” I think that the dichotomy of what she believes in her heart and wants to be true and what she spouts in front of people, I sort of think both things are true at once, and I think that’s just the kind of human element.

But I also think that it’s vital to remember in that monologue that Charlie really pulls it out of her. She really doesn’t want to do the dance, the dancing monkey, or what did she say? “There’s a dancing bear aspect to your request,” I think is such a great line. But yeah, I think both things are true for her.

You have the sense she’s mentioned this speech before, and again, maybe she doesn’t totally believe it, but Charlie just loves it and so she has to do it.

Sources indicate that david and I spoke about it a lot, and we sort of landed on we feel like she did it once off the cuff, like at a table at the Emmys or the Globes, and everyone went, “Gee, Karen, that’s genius.” And Charlie heard it and went, “Yeah, that’s genius. She’s my agent, look how smart she is. She’s so great.” Then she’s done it one other time at a dinner. So, by the time we get to the pool, she’s like, “Oh, my God.” It’s becoming a routine against her will, which was also a really fun element to play with in terms of how much she does or doesn’t enjoy it, and finding that balance.

Do you personally read reviews of your work?

Has that always been the case for you?

Has it always been the case? [Smiles] I’m sure anyone who doesn’t read a review once read a bad review.

It doesn’t even have to be a bad one. What I learned is, you can read a review that is seemingly positive, but it might not be what you were trying to do, and then you feel heartbroken about that too. So yes, I really avoid it. Yeah.

You get to slap Brad Pitt a lot in this film. Was that hard to do?

Industry observers note that it’s a very beautiful face, and we had to do it. We had to do it. And Brad is a very good sport and a very good stuntman. I think that Brad was very, very comfortable, and I was very nervous. We shot the dialogue for two days, that we were just in almost this sort of trance of the two of them, and of the very unusual power dynamic that [they have]. One of the best things about that scene to me, which I didn’t analyze at the time, it’s so intricate the way that Quentin wrote it. It’s this moment where, in revealing what he wants, he becomes so vulnerable that the power dynamic kind of very subtly shifts in this kind of core foundational way between these two characters.

So, we shot that for two days and then all of a sudden it was like, “Oh, my God, it ends, and I need to figure out how to do this.” We had an amazing stunt coordinator on that job.

We had to do extremely complex things with people, but with me, I was like, “Hey Dave, could we just pop out the back there and have a little chat about the slap…?”.

In a recent development, everyone knows that David likes to do a lot of takes. How many takes was the actual slapping?

Not so many! It was probably the least amount of takes we did. We probably did a couple, five, maybe six. And then I do remember that Brad sort of went, “OK, I think we got it. I think we’re good now,” and we moved on. But we did the inside [slap] first. It was such a joy to do. It’s such a happy memory. We filmed it, and then we all ran around to the monitor, and we watched it in playback, and we’re like, “Oh, my God, it’s so good.” And then we filmed it again. We were so pleased with ourselves. [Laughs].

What scenes did David ask for the most takes?

The thing about the takes is, it’s coverage-dependent. So, if you have four actors in a scene, like the hamburger monologue, let’s say there’s four setups on each actor, you do 10 takes per setup. So, that becomes a lot.

I will say that in the pig speech monologue, I don’t have a lot of lines, but we did just as much coverage on me as we did on Brad and Scott. That was one of my first days on set, and I remember thinking, “This is so, so unusual. Why is he doing this?” And then a couple weeks later, he highlighted me a kind of rough edit, and I thought, “Oh, my God, that’s why he did it.” He is using Karen as the kind of go-between. As David would always say, at least there’s one grown-up in the room, and it’s Karen.

Industry observers note that so I do have this really funny memory too of doing that during the pig monologue scene. I was off-camera, or we were catching just the side of me; I was very much out of focus, and I took a drag of the cigarette, and I remember he gave me a note for that, something about the speed of it or the intention of it. And I remember thinking ….

Sources indicate that exactly! I was like, “You saw that?” And he was right, he was absolutely right, but I thought, “OK, this is not a set where we get away with anything.”.

Especially in that scene, you have these facial expressions where you are having the appropriate reaction to what we’re hearing, but in such a beautiful way. I think that’s when we all fall in love with Karen. We’re like, “She gets it. She knows how ridiculous this is,” but she is part of this world.

Industry observers note that I’m particularly proud of the Tic Tac crunch; that was my prop idea, and I just thought we should end with her crunching down on something, because she’s so pissed about having to then go and spend her entire morning looking for a hog in Malibu Colony or something. Where is she even going to find that pig?

Industry observers note that she did it. I mean, David and I would talk about that too. I’m like, “Do you think she did it or she sent Mallory, her assistant, to go do it?” Either way, someone did it, someone paid for it.

Recent findings suggest that speaking of falling in love with Karen, there’s been this sentiment circulating as people see the film that there is a real rom-com built into it with Cliff and Karen. Do you see it that way?

I don’t think it’s a rom-com, but I think it’s romantic, and I think they’re funny. Don’t get me wrong, rom-coms are my religion. Yesterday I was walking through Latest York, and I literally felt like I was in “You’ve Got Mail.” I was like, “This fall day, I need a bunch of sharpened pencils.” But I don’t think that this necessarily falls into that category. It’s sort of undefinable, indefinable, but I do think it’s really romantic. I felt that when we were playing it, and we really enjoyed that together.

The romance of it is kind of surprising, because it surprises her. It’s sort of best case scenario romance, that you think you have it all together, and this person walks in that you absolutely dismiss in terms of that, and then little by little they just sort of reveal this thing. More beautifully, they pull something out of you. I didn’t necessarily intellectualize any of this while we were shooting it, it’s just that I can see that now retrospectively. Not that I read anything, but I am curious what people will make of them.

Netflix will release “The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth” in IMAX theaters on Wednesday, November 25. It will be available to stream on Netflix starting Wednesday, December 23.

25 Years Later, GTA 3 Is Still the Most Fascinating Open-World Experiment

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1491 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Polygon

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that it’s October 2001, and you’re standing in a dimly lit game store, where rows upon rows of boxes sit in anticipation as you glance across their titles, unsure exactly which among them you'll end up taking home.
  • In a recent development, the artwork’s nothing to write home about, just a collage of pictures in red, blue, and green hues, featuring obscure faces, a police chopper, and a car up in flames.
  • Grand Theft Auto 3 was a jolt of raw adrenaline.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that it’s October 2001, and you’re standing in a dimly lit game store, where rows upon rows of boxes sit in anticipation as you glance across their titles, unsure exactly which among them you'll end up taking home. Unfortunately, you can only pick one. Your eyes are already darting between Devil May Cry, Silent Hill 2, and Ico, which all feel eerily attuned to those pre-Halloween vibes. Noticing your indecisiveness (and the look of impatience on your mother’s face), the store clerk strides over with an assist, placing in your hands a game you had never heard of until that very moment.

In a recent development, the artwork’s nothing to write home about, just a collage of pictures in red, blue, and green hues, featuring obscure faces, a police chopper, and a car up in flames. Your instinct is to just go with your gut; Silent Hill 2 is what you came here for, after all. But something’s telling you otherwise. Maybe it’s the store clerk going on about its open-world premise, or the name itself that strikes a chord within you. Whatever reason incites it, you make the ultimate decision. Little did you know, you’d be walking home with one of the greatest achievements in video game history.

Grand Theft Auto 3 was a jolt of raw adrenaline. It was a paradigm shift that made the possibilities of 3D open-world design feel almost limitless. The game thrust players into what Rockstar co-founder Dan Houser described as “an old, post-industrial American city,” a mash-up of Chicago, Pittsburgh, Detroit, Philly, and mostly Latest York teeming with grim alleyways, pedestrian-filled streets, and sky-slicing buildings that eclipsed many of the incredible worlds that came before it, from The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time to Driver. It was called Liberty City. No game had molded such immense verticality into a 3D world that felt like a living ecosystem where the inhabitants and environments reacted to you directly. It was a feat many at the time considered impossible on existing hardware — and Rockstar did it with virtually no load times to boot.

In a recent development, like nearly every title the studio would develop for the system, GTA 3 pushed the PlayStation 2 to its absolute limits. Developers DMA Design (now known as Rockstar North) had to cleverly stream around 130MB of data, including 3D animations, textures, models, and audio, through the PS2’s 32MB of system RAM. For perspective, just one Liberty City island amounted to roughly 50MB of static geometry. To make it all work, the team engineered a dynamic streaming system that fetched sectors of the map ahead of the player, while purging the city behind them. It’s why you’d often see the city pop in and populate right in front of you if you were driving at top speeds and rapidly looked behind the character. When code couldn't bridge the gap, Rockstar cleverly designed curved roads to slow down sports cars, added subtle aerodynamic drag to prevent vehicles from outrunning the laser reader, and capped active traffic to eight models. What technical leads Adam Fowler, Obbe Vermeij, and their colleagues accomplished with GTA 3 was nothing short of magic.

Technical limitations weren’t the only roadblocks for Rockstar. Following the release of GTA 2, which he felt suffered from a lack of narrative thrust due to its non-linear design, Houser set out to give GTA 3 a far more complex story. With the help of co-writer James Worrall, they devised localized character "hubs" that served as contacts for missions, like Joey Leone, Toni Cipriani, and Salvatore Leone. Rather than treating open-world freedom and story progression as opposing forces, Houser used these dynamic webs to bridge the gap, tying mission arcs directly to specific territories and turf wars. That allowed GTA 3’s story to organically teach players the city's layouts and mechanics, moving through the industrial side of Portland with Toni Cipriani, navigating the Leone family's criminal empire with Salvatore, and eventually venturing into Staunton Island's political corruption and corporate underbelly. Each newly introduced contact pulled Claude deeper into Liberty City's criminal ecosystem, gradually opening up new territories while revealing another layer of the city's interconnected underworld. Coupled with the decision to keep Claude a silent protagonist, the hub structure allowed players to chart their own path without sacrificing the momentum of a cohesive crime saga.

It has been revealed that the radio stations of GTA 3 also gave it that extra level of immersion, but before Rockstar could throw cash at some of the biggest names in the industry, the developers had to improvise with completely original music. Led by audio directors Craig Conner and Stuart Ross, the team wrote and recorded genre-specific tracks under aliases, like “Lucy,” “The Mudds,” “Marydances,” “Da Shootaz,” and more. Ross and Conner were also responsible for the GTA 3 Main Theme, a moody, “dark jazz” track inspired by The Sopranos and Goodfellas, which is still one of the best in the series. Combining underground hip-hop, drum & bass, and licensed classics from Giorgio Moroder’s Scarface score, the team was able to capture a gritty realism in the sounds of Liberty City. It’s a testament to Rockstar’s sonic ingenuity, one that finds a kind of spiritual successor in GTA 6, which features original scoring by French electronic duo Justice. The tools have changed, but the underlying idea remains the same: original music can give a fictional city an identity all its own.

What elevated these stations even further was GTA’s name-brand comedy, still in its infancy but just as hilarious, brought to life in Chatterbox FM. Scripted by Houser and hosted by Lazlow Jones, the talk-radio station's absurd caller rants and SNL-like commercial parodies gave Liberty City a lived-in texture long before you ever stepped out of your (likely stolen) vehicle. An especially on-the-nose example is a first-time-caller mother who rants about parenting in the age of video games: “I let my kid play video games, and now he runs around the house looking for gold coins. This is teaching our children to go chase money!” One of my personal favorites involves a suitably redneck-sounding character raving about how “guns don’t kill people, death kills people.” They go on to add: “You can’t die from a bullet, you can die from a cardiac arrest or organ failure or major hemorrhage. Small piece of metal ain’t the problem.” It’s no wonder Chatterbox is still widely considered some of the funniest and most satirical writing in the entire GTA series, though GTA 6 is shaping up to give GTA 3 a run for its comedy gold.

A weekly cheat sheet to what you’ll eventually love to play. No buying, no commitment — just saving for later.

Industry observers note that on the heels of 9/11, released just 41 days after those fatal terrorist attacks, GTA 3 also remains a strange time capsule. Rockstar delayed the game by a few weeks to surgically scrub dialogue and a mission referencing terrorism, and changed the city’s squad cars from blue-and-white NYPD knockoffs to generic black-and-whites. Even the original box art was scrapped in North America, giving birth to the now-iconic grid layout that emblazons the cover of every series follow-up. Yet beyond those surface-level tweaks, the game took on a surreal weight in the wake of the tragedy. Having grown up just across the river in New Jersey, the attacks were an inextricable part of my life, even if much of the chaos of that era remains a blur. But I’ll never forget the long nights spent driving through Liberty City in the shadow of such devastation. Steering through those dark and rainy streets felt hauntingly poignant; a digital New York pulsing with life at a moment when the real world had suddenly ground to a painful halt.

According to recent reports, GTA 3 was a baseball bat to the face of the gaming industry at a time when it was flourishing. It landed in the same year as Ico, Silent Hill 2, Halo: Combat Evolved, Final Fantasy 10, and Metal Gear Solid 2. Even in the face of such greatness, Grand Theft Auto 3 is unparalleled in its scope, bridging some of the most sophisticated world design ever attempted with a bespoke narrative engine that forever changed gaming. No one noted it better than Sam Houser, who told IGN in 2001: “It has its own personality in a way I've never seen before in a game, to the point where it actually becomes part of the gameplay experience.”.

It has been revealed that personality. That's what has always made Grand Theft Auto one of the most compelling entertainment properties on the planet, and GTA 3 was where that personality truly came into its own. 25 years later, with Rockstar's dominant open-world adventure being the latest example, Liberty City remains a testament to how ambition and clever design can fundamentally reshape an entire medium.

The Substantial Game is coming to the Big Screen. Technically the biggest screens.

Super Bowl LXI is set to play live on IMAX screens across North America, as well as in some international markets, specifically Australia, New Zealand, and Brazil. The game takes place on Sunday, February 14, 2027, or Valentine’s Day 2027, and now you can convince your partner that the Valentine’s Day date night is still alive because you can go out to the movie theater to watch the game instead of stay at home.

Industry observers note that IMAX will screen everything from the pregame and postgame coverage, the full four-hour presentation of the game itself, and of course the Halftime Show headlined by Jay-Z, all beginning at 6 pm ET. According to recent reports, tickets are expected to go on sale in January. Specific theater locations and ticketing information will be confirmed in the coming weeks.

Sources indicate that this is the first time IMAX is screening something as substantial as the Super Bowl, but it’s not the first time IMAX has played live sporting events in its theaters. IMAX also screened the opening ceremony for the Paris Olympics, it this year did a series of F1 races in partnership with Apple TV, and events like NHL games and even the NBA Finals have played internationally. This is on a much bigger scale as well, as this will be available in hundreds of IMAX screens across the country.

ABC, Disney, and ESPN hadn’t been in the rotation for the Super Bowl for a long time, so they’ve been going all out for their first go around. Disney is making the game available via broadcast on ABC, as well as on ESPN and Univision, and also for streaming on Disney+. ESPN is also doing an alternate telecast on ESPN 2 with Peyton and Eli Manning as they do for “Monday Night Football” throughout the regular season. And it was previously announced that “The Pat McAfee Show” is getting in on the fun with its own Super Bowl show on ESPNU and “Playbook with Next Gen Stats” on NFL Network.

Recent findings suggest that this is really a boon for theaters to do added business on a day and weekend when most theaters are pretty empty and the newly introduced movie options are few and far between. We’ll see though how the box office responds and how many people relocate their Super Bowl parties to their local multiplex.

Sources indicate that “Watching the Super Bowl with your fellow fans is one of the great shared experiences in sports, and this first-of-its-kind collaboration with the NFL and IMAX takes it to a historic new scale,” said Ken Potrock, President, Major Event Integration for The Walt Disney Manufacturer. “With ESPN’s first Super Bowl, we’re reaching fans across an unprecedented range of platforms and meeting them wherever they want to be, with unique moments that only Disney and ESPN can deliver.”.

Recent findings suggest that “The Super Bowl is a one-of-a-kind global cultural event imbued with spectacle, sound, drama, and heroes — all the makings of a great IMAX experience,” mentioned Rich Gelfond, CEO of IMAX. “This is a milestone for IMAX that further elevates our standing as a premier global platform for entertainment and events, and we’re excited to work in partnership with Disney, ESPN and the NFL to give football fans an unforgettable night.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that the concept of multiversal and all-encompassing threats among DC Comics' biggest, baddest villains has expanded since the days of enemies like the Anti-Monitor's introduction. Villains of this scope can regularly become far more terrifying than one singular hero can take, whether it's the current and looming danger of Darkseid's full physical return, or other interstellar menaces. And, while it often takes the might of the Justice League and frequently other forces to keep them at bay, Superman regularly stands among the greatest of their heroes against these existential terrors. Now, over 25 years later, one such danger appears to resurface.

According to recent reports, in the latest solicits for Justice League Unlimited #28, Mark Waid and Dan Mora's run teases the return of the primordial embodiment of entropy, Imperiex. The cover art alone features the imposing profile and distinctive armor of Imperiex behind DC's Trinity as they carry out the next steps in stopping Darkseid's impending return. But as they go to direct the tidal waves of massive war from crushing Earth, they soon find their next destination already inundated with dangers of its own. With Superman having led the charge alongside surprising momentary allies to defeat Imperiex before, the question arises whether he can do the same against such an immensely strong foe once more.

It has been revealed that with Superman being joined by a large coalition of allies including the surprising aid of Darkseid and Lex Luthor to defeat Imperiex and Brainiac 13 in Action Comics #782, it seems unlikely a similar turnout will occur this time around. In fact, Darkseid is actively preparing for threats of Imperiex's scale, knowing well that cosmic figures like him are among the few who could actually stop his own spin on a Massive Bang-level multiversal event. The glitch teasing Imperiex's real return appears to be Justice League Unlimited #28, with him possibly being the leading figure behind the sudden invasion of the New Gods' homeworld.

BEGINNING A FIVE-PART EPIC WAR STORY! In order to save the Earth from Darkseid's coming threat, the League will have to move the battlefield to Latest Genesis, once home to the New Gods — now overrun with tens of thousands of deadly alien invaders serving an unknown master of incalculable power! With little hope of victory, the League has no choice but to wage war on a scale so vast, there will be losses that will change the DC Universe!

Industry observers note that the solicits tease that, in preparing to avoid war ravaging Earth, they appear to have descended into the belly of the beast, specifically one who wields the energy sufficient to generate his own Substantial Bangs. Glimpses of Imperiex have been sparse even in peripheral stories like Injustice, or even crossovers like Scooby Doo! and Scribblenauts Unmasked: A DC Comics Adventure, so this latest return will re-establish just how dangerous he is.

It's fair to say Imperiex will once again be more than merely Superman can handle, but he'll doubtlessly be at the forefront, trying to prevent wanton disaster before the one they're already trying to stay ahead of. With Imperiex perfectly fitting the bill of a being carrying incalculable power, and his presence gracing the latest cover art, it's mostly a question of exactly how he comes back, and what his return will do to the DC Universe.

According to recent reports, it's pretty reasonable to say multiple generations of DC Comics fans can now point to an event that reshaped the DC Universe before. Usually their common tell is the word "Crisis" somewhere, or something bearing similar levels of urgency. Even subsequent limited series like 52 addressed the ripple effects of said changes, producing some truly memorable stories and putting the spotlight on underappreciated heroes. With threats emerging on multiple fronts, none of which leaving much hope for Earth or much of the universe's survival, it'll be interesting to see what this crisis' codename will end up being.

But the other enticing aspect of this upcoming glitch, set for February 24, 2027, means that over 25 years later, the most iconic members of the DC superheroes' pantheon will potentially be fighting Imperiex once again. The cover art alone is an enticing glimpse of what's to come, with figures like Doctor Occult's presence being an intriguing enough mystery in terms of their roles, while Newly introduced Gods like Orion are confirmed to make an appearance, while the Hellbat Armor's scenery-chewing return will surely turn heads in the internals. While Superman may not have the same allies at his back against Imperiex this time, he'll still nonetheless not face him alone.

While the Duo is open, the outer screen can mirror Halide’s camera controls or show a full-screen viewfinder without controls. The second option lets the person you’re photographing see how you’ve framed the shot.

Industry observers note that in low light, Halide can use the outer screen as a fill flash. That gives you a softer source of light for portraits, and Halide’s developers recommend turning the screen brightness all the way up before taking the photo.

It has been revealed that halide also now places the histogram along the Duo’s crease. The update revises the Photo Lab interface for editing with the Duo half open as well.

On other iPhones, Halide 3.4 restores the color and luminance histograms and the shutter timer from Mark II.

In a recent development, halide Mark III launched back in May with a redesigned camera and the latest Photo Lab editor. Recent updates added RAW-only capture in 3.1 and Aperture Priority for iPhone 18 Pro in 3.2. Halide Mark III version 3.4 is available now on the App Store.

Why Black Friday and Cyber Monday Are Bad Days to Impulse Buy Electronics

  • It's Cyber Monday, and Lifehacker is sharing the best sales based on product reviews and comparisons before the sales are over.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Black Friday sales officially start Friday, November 28, and run through Cyber Monday, November 30, 2026, and Lifehacker is sharing the best sales based on product reviews and comparisons before it's over.

It's Cyber Monday, and Lifehacker is sharing the best sales based on product reviews and comparisons before the sales are over.

Sales are accurate at the time of publication, but prices and inventory are always subject to change.

Not every Black Friday or Cyber Monday deal is as sweet as it seems. With electronics and tech in particular, you could be buying last year's model that has actually been on sale since the summer—and was maybe a better price a few months ago. Here’s how to avoid impulse buying a misleading Black Friday “deal” and make sure you’re getting the best bang for your buck.

Recent findings suggest that when you see products like food, clothes, or home goods with a major "Black Friday" or "Cyber Monday" tag slapped on them, it's probably safe to take advantage of that deal. Chances are it's the same exact product you'd find on other days of the year. The same can’t be remarked for a TV, laptop, and other tech deals, where the product itself is constantly being upgraded.

Because tech is always evolving, and retailers want to move inventory before new models come out, electronics are especially susceptible to a practice known as "price anchoring." That's when retailers mark up prices in the weeks leading up to Black Friday, before "slashing" those prices back down, giving the appearance of a deal that isn't really a deal at all. Still, when you see that marked-up number, aka the "price anchor," you might get tricked into thinking you're saving money when you're not. There's also the false sense of urgency that gets created. It's second nature to assume that anything labeled "deal" won’t last long—even when this so-called deal price has actually been going on since the summer.

Industry observers note that price anchoring isn't even unique to Black Friday. The nonprofit Consumers’ Checkbook tracked prices at 25 major retailers over 33 weeks in 2022 and found that more than half the items tracked were offered at false discounts every week or almost every week. Less common, but also worth noting, is a known practice of "derivative" or retailer-exclusive models produced specifically for the holiday shopping season. These versions often feature cheaper components, fewer features, or lower specifications than their regular counterparts. A 55-inch TV from a reputable brand might look identical to the year-round model, but it could have a lower refresh rate, inferior panel technology, or fewer HDMI ports.

In the same vein, that "amazing deal" on a laptop might come with last year's processor, or a smartphone that's about to be replaced. The matter isn't that the tech is an older model, but again, it's that it probably has been at this low a price, or lower, since the summer. Alternatively, some deeply discounted electronics are refurbished units or open-box returns that have been repackaged. Again, while this isn't necessarily a bad thing, impulse buyers may not fully realize what they're buying.

Sources indicate that the key phrasing here is impulse buying. Events like Black Friday are psychologically engineered to trigger impulse purchases. Limited-time offers, countdown clocks, and "while supplies last" warnings create artificial urgency. When you're caught up in the moment, it's easy to convince yourself you need a upcoming tablet, smartwatch, or gaming console, even if you hadn't considered buying one before.

To avoid a low-key scam, do your research. The easiest way to tell that you’re getting the correct product is by checking the model or serial number. And with online shopping, finding and double-checking those numbers is quick and easy. In addition, don't just compare prices—compare specs. Look at processor speeds, RAM, storage capacity, screen resolution, refresh rates, and connectivity options. A $300 laptop isn't a deal if a slightly more expensive model offers significantly better performance that will last longer.

If you do see a deal that catches your eye, it could pay to wait. Cyber Monday, post-Christmas sales, and even January clearances often feature electronics deals that rival or beat Black Friday prices, all without the famous chaos and pressure. Then again, you risk more “out-of-stock” results if you wait, so the risk is up to you, depending on the popularity of the item you’re eyeing (and how badly you want it).

The bottom line: Don’t fall victim to a falsely advertised lower-quality product, and do a little research to find actually good deals ahead of time.

Yes, Amazon has Black Friday sales, and we vet our deals to make sure they’re the best ones. You can also refer to guides like our live blog that have already done all of the vetting for you. And if you have an Amazon Prime membership, make the most of it.

Recent findings suggest that nowadays, both large retailers and small businesses compete for Black Friday shoppers, so you can expect practically every store to run sales through Monday, November 30, 2026. The “best” sales depend on your needs, but in general, the biggest discounts tend to come from larger retailers who can afford lower prices: think places like Amazon, Walmart, Target, Best Buy, and Home Depot. You can find all the best sales from major retailers on our Black Friday coverage.

Yes. Walmart, Best Buy, Target, and Home Depot will all have in-store deals, some of which you might not find online, so if you're able to take a trip to your local retailer, keep your eyes open for different deals.

In a recent development, yes, Apple participates in Black Friday, though you may want to compare their sales with other retailers like Best Buy and Walmart. So far, the best Black Friday sale on an Apple product is the M5 MacBook Air on sale for $200 off, the lowest price since the price hike this summer.

Black Friday sales officially begin Friday, November 27, 2026, and run throughout “Cyber Week,” the five-day period that runs from Thanksgiving through Cyber Monday,  November 30, 2026. But Black Friday and Cyber Monday dates have expanded as retailers compete for customers. You can get the same Black Friday sales early, and we expect sales to wind down by December 2, 2026.

  • Director Andrey Zvyagintsev has worked with supervising re-recording mixer Andrey Dergachev for 20 years, since the director’s second film, “Banishment.” On each project, including their most recent portrait of a rotten marriage in a rotten world, “Minotaur,” they’ve tried to improve the sound design—using it as a hook that makes the film’s world feel more vital and alive for the audience.
  • This is never more true than in the absurdly sad and funny, then suddenly murderous confrontation between cuckolded husband Gleb (Dmitriy Mazurov) and his wife’s lover Anton (Yuriy Zavalnyouk) at the hinge point of “Minotaur.” Related Stories Super Bowl LXI to Play Live on IMAX Screens ‘Cliff Booth’ Star Elizabeth Debicki on Slapping Brad Pitt, ‘The Movie Critic,’ and the Rom-Com Question.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Editor’s Note: This article contains spoilers for “Minotaur.”.

Director Andrey Zvyagintsev has worked with supervising re-recording mixer Andrey Dergachev for 20 years, since the director’s second film, “Banishment.” On each project, including their most recent portrait of a rotten marriage in a rotten world, “Minotaur,” they’ve tried to improve the sound design—using it as a hook that makes the film’s world feel more vital and alive for the audience.

Seriously, spoilers. This is never more true than in the absurdly sad and funny, then suddenly murderous confrontation between cuckolded husband Gleb (Dmitriy Mazurov) and his wife’s lover Anton (Yuriy Zavalnyouk) at the hinge point of “Minotaur.” Related Stories Super Bowl LXI to Play Live on IMAX Screens ‘Cliff Booth’ Star Elizabeth Debicki on Slapping Brad Pitt, ‘The Movie Critic,’ and the Rom-Com Question.

According to recent reports, zvyagintsev and Dergachev generally strive to preserve as much authentic production sound from performances as possible. “On my third movie, ‘Elena,’ we recorded the live sound from shooting, and it’s maybe two or three phrases we had to rerecord, but otherwise the whole sound that you hear is fully recorded during the shooting,” Zvyagintsev told IndieWire on an upcoming episode of the Filmmaker Toolkit podcast. “Our main purpose is to keep as much sound from the shooting as possible and not to add anything extra, and it was the same for ‘Minotaur.’”.

It has been revealed that but for the moment that Gleb attacks Anton, and its aftermath, it was notable to Zvyagintsev that the world beyond the apartment start intruding on Gleb — that even though he wants desperately to cover up what he’s done and make sure no one sees or learns about it, we hear dozens of ways in which he isn’t alone. That required a lot of work outside of the studio to record the background noises Zvyagintsev and Dergachev could then layer into the scene.

In a recent development, “We were creating [background] sounds of the kids playing football in the backyard. We would spend the whole day recording the kids, how they’re speaking, the way they’re playing, people passing by on the street,” Zvyagintsev noted. They also recorded different sound layers from Gleb’s luxury SUV, which they could deploy to create maximum panic in both Gleb and the audience.

“The car signals, the leaves on the street, the birds — they all pronounced, and [emphasized] something. So we were modulating all those layers that we recorded, and then we combined them to create the atmosphere and to put it all in one place for the scene,” Zvyagintsev noted.

Industry observers note that there’s atmosphere from outside and from inside, as Zvyagintsev and Dergachev refused to let Gleb have a moment of peace on the soundtrack — until, as with all the cruel jokes of “Minotaur’s” filmmaking, he gets it in the worst way, at the worst possible moment. There’s a terrible silence once he’s struck Anton on the head with his own camera. And then the world comes rushing back in, even louder than before.

“We were trying to create this volume of sounds right after the hit. And then, when Anton is falling, there is this complete silence. And then somewhere far away we hear the car alarm and even more sounds that create this volume. This is what we were looking for,” Zvyagintsev said.

Industry observers note that it was key to finesse the sound design of the sequence so as not to overplay it. Zvyagintsev initially wanted to add music to the moment, but had to hold himself back. “It was really tempting,” Zvyagintsev noted. “My composer Evgueni Galperine even wrote the music, which we added. But when we saw the result, we realized, and I understood that no, no, it has to be completely silent.”.

It has been revealed that silent as the grave, one might say. But it’s the sound design, the modulation between loudness and silence, that makes the moment so horrifying. Zvyagintsev and Dergachev did it by hand, just to make sure of it.

“Minotaur” is now playing in select theaters.

According to recent reports, you can cancel your Prime subscription via web browser by first logging into your Amazon account. Amazon has a Cancel Your Prime Membership button on its support page to launch the process, or you can follow the steps detailed on Amazon's page:.

Head to Amazon.com in your web browser.

Hover over the Accounts & Lists menu on the top-right of the window, then select the Prime Membership option.

Then tap the End Your Amazon Prime Membership button and finally click the Cancel Your Prime Membership orange button.

Follow the on-screen instructions to cancel your Prime subscription.

Note that Amazon requires a bunch of clicks to finalize your cancellation, giving you lots of “opportunities” to change your mind.

Open the Amazon Shopping app on your mobile device.

Click the three horizontal lines on the bottom right.

Under Shop by Category, select Prime.

On the top bar, slide all the way to the end and select Help.

Then tap the End Your Amazon Prime Membership button and finally click the Cancel Your Prime Membership orange button.

Follow the on-screen instructions to cancel your Prime subscription.

As mentioned, closing your account will immediately end your access. Amazon also offers you the option to pause your benefits and billing temporarily instead of canceling them completely. Either way, your Amazon account is still active—you simply won’t have Prime benefits.

According to recent reports, finally, if you have other subscriptions connected to your Prime account, those will end when your billing is up. And if you signed up for Prime through the Android mobile shopping app or the Prime Video Android app, you’ll have to go through Google Subscription to manage your membership.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that after 13 long years, the wait is finally over, and like many of you, I couldn’t wait to load up GTA 6 for the first time this weekend. However, instead of playing on the largest screen in my house, I decided that a pair of AR glasses might be the best way to experience this fresh and improved Vice City. Let me explain.

With a game this massive and this anticipated, the last thing you want is to be interrupted — or worse, unable to play because someone else in your household claimed the TV first. Now, if you’re an adult who lives by yourself and got to play GTA 6 sprawled out on your couch with one of the best OLED TVs, more power to you.

It has been revealed that for those of us with a significant other or kids at home, though, carving out the necessary time to finally play GTA 6 hasn’t been that easy. Fortunately for me, I knew there was another way instead of trying to sneak in a late-night play session in front of the TV.

It has been revealed that you see, over the summer on a trip to Taiwan for Computex, I spent almost my entire 17-hour flight playing Red Dead Redemption on the Switch 2 in AR glasses. That got me thinking: what if I tried playing GTA 6 the same way? Well, that’s exactly what I did, and I don’t think I’d be nearly as far in the game right now if I hadn’t.

Here’s why you, too, might want to consider donning a pair of AR glasses—or more accurately, display glasses — to take in the sights, sounds, and excitement that Vice City has to offer in GTA 6.

Sources indicate that this bundle has everything you need to start playing your game consoles in AR. You get a pair of Viture Pro 2 XR glasses and the Viture Pro Mobile Dock. This way you can plug your Switch 2 in directly over USB-C or consoles like the PS5 or Xbox Series X in over HDMI and the included dock brings big-screen console gaming right to your glasses. Alternatively, if you only plan on playing your Switch 2 this way, you can pick up the Viture Pro 2 Mini Dock Pack for $375 (down from 428) right now.

With a gaming PC or even a handheld like the Steam Deck, playing with AR glasses is as simple as plugging them in. On a console, though, it’s not that easy. Fortunately, Viture makes a few accessories to help.

For instance, there’s the Viture Pro Mobile Dock and the fresh Viture Mobile Dock Mini. While I played RDR using the latter, when I tried playing my Switch 2 in AR glasses back at launch, I used the former. Don’t get me wrong, the new mini dock is super compact and easier to bring with you, but for playing on any console besides the Nintendo Switch, it’s missing one very important port: HDMI.

Get instant access to breaking news, the hottest reviews, great deals and helpful tips.

Sources indicate that now with the Pro Mobile Dock, in addition to USB-C out ports for two pairs of glasses — and a USB-C input for devices like the Switch 2 — you also get a full-sized HDMI port. Admittedly, I didn’t have a use for it before as I’ve mainly played games in AR glasses while traveling or on vacation, but with my PS5 Pro fired up with GTA 6 installed and ready to go, it was time to put it to the test.

I ran a long HDMI cable from the back of my console, plugged it into the dock along with a pair of the Viture Pro 2 AR glasses, powered it on, and I was good to go. GTA 6 appeared almost instantly on the Micro-OLED displays in the glasses, and since they have built-in speakers, that was all I needed.

Industry observers note that although I love their more affordable $299 price, Viture did have to cut one of my favorite features from its other glasses. Unlike the tech giant’s other models — and this is true with the Xreal XBX A01 glasses, too — there isn’t any built-in electrochromic dimming. Instead, you get a lens shade in the box.

Now, if you’ve never worn a pair of AR glasses before, electrochromic dimming lets you go from a clear display where you can see the world around you (in addition to the content from your game console, phone, or tablet) to a dimmed one without ambient light seeping through, all with the push of a button.

The Viture Pro 2 glasses do have one feature going for them that made my GTA 6 play sessions a whole lot more comfortable, though. They’re extremely lightweight at just 63 grams.

Playing GTA 6 with AR glasses felt just like making my way through the Wild West as John Marston in RDR. I was able to take in all of Leonida without bothering anyone else in my house, and since the game runs at 30 fps, I didn’t lose anything when it came to visual quality. Now, if I were playing on PC, that would be a different story, since the Pro 2s come equipped with a 120Hz refresh rate — making them just as good for fast-paced games as they are for slower ones.

If you want to try something similar, you’ll get the best experience using the Pro Mobile Dock — or better yet, Viture’s new HDMI to USB-C adapter cable. Mine is still in the mail, though, so I made do with the Pro Mobile Dock, and for now, everything worked exceptionally well. However, that isn’t the only way to play GTA 6 in AR glasses.

Besides using Viture’s AR glasses with one of its docks, I’ve also spent a fair amount of time playing on a smartphone, too. If you have a newer iPhone, Samsung phone, or any smartphone with DisplayPort Alt Mode over USB-C, you just plug your glasses in and you’re good to go. With that kind of setup, you can load up a remote play app like PXPlay (for PlayStation) or XBXPlay (for Xbox) and use a wireless controller.

That does leave your phone just lying there, which is why Viture teamed up with 8BitDo a while back to create a variant of the 8BitDo Ultimate Mobile Gaming Controller with a full-featured USB-C port. On most mobile game controllers, the USB-C ports are just used for passthrough charging. With this one, though, you can plug in a pair of AR glasses and actually get video out.

Just like I did during my second long-haul flight to Taiwan a few years back, I popped my Samsung Galaxy S24 FE into the controller and plugged in my AR glasses. After getting PXPlay set up on that phone, I was able to use remote play on my PS5 Pro to play GTA 6 in bed.

It has been revealed that as I was fixing up Jason’s house, though, I noticed that it was slightly difficult to see and read the button prompts on the edges of the screen. Since this was my first time playing GTA 6, I had no idea which button to press when using a nail gun to hang drywall or to fix the shingles on my roof. So I put the Pro 2s down and switched to the Viture Luma Pro glasses instead.

According to recent reports, with the simple mission of giving you the best bang for your buck in AR glasses, Viture knocked it out the park with Luma Pro. These have the best color science of any glasses on this list, and there’s versatility in the Spacewalker software to turn any space into a giant 152-inch panoramic workspace with 3DoF tracking that keeps it anchored.

With their higher-resolution lenses (from 1080p per eye to 1200p), wider field of view (from 46 to 52 degrees), and redesigned optical stack, what was blurry on the Pro 2s became instantly clear on the Luma Pros. Now, if you’re on a tight budget and already know the controls, you can still definitely play GTA 6 with the Pro 2s. However, since I was newly introduced to the controls and had both pairs of glasses handy, making the switch was easy and absolutely worthwhile.

In a recent development, one feature that you’ll find on both pairs of glasses — and pretty much the rest of the AR glasses in Viture’s lineup — are myopia dials. With these, you can turn the dials to go from a blurry to a clear picture if, like me, you wear glasses or contacts. Most of the time I wear contacts, and I make it a point to have them in when wearing AR glasses. However, since I wanted to play in bed, I decided this was finally the time to try them out.

Now, I had to fully light the room in the pictures above, but on Friday and Saturday — and hopefully on Sunday evening once I’m done writing this — I cozied up in bed with that special 8BitDo controller and my AR glasses and played more GTA 6 than I’d like to admit. And frankly, it was awesome.

At first, I was a bit worried about the remote play experience with such a complex game, but with one of the best mesh Wi-Fi systems equipped with Wi-Fi 7 and a fast internet connection, it worked really well.

It has been revealed that now, I did have my PS5 Pro plugged into my router with an Ethernet cable during those play sessions. However, when I took the pics above, I had it unplugged, and that tanked the game’s performance. So if you want to play GTA 6 remotely — with or without AR glasses — I strongly recommend connecting your console over Ethernet for a smoother and more stable remote play experience.

It has been revealed that as I’m also currently testing out the Viture Pro Neckband, I decided to put it on and go play outside for a bit of fun. While the device around my neck might look like a wearable fan, it’s actually a wearable Android tablet, if you can believe it.

In a recent development, now, what I like about this setup compared to using the Pro Mobile Dock or a smartphone is that my hands weren’t weighed down and I wasn’t tethered to my console. Likewise, if you’re using a third-party app like PXPlay, you can use whatever controller you want and aren’t limited to just using a wired DualSense (like you are on PC).

Recent findings suggest that now, I must say that playing GTA 6 wasn’t nearly as good on the Pro Neckband as it was on a smartphone. Still, with my Eero Outdoor 7 mesh node on the fence behind me and seated in The Foldable Gaming Chair, it was quite comfy and still very playable. If only the weather had been Vice City sunny instead of overcast.

It has been revealed that with a pair of AR glasses and the right dock — or even a capable smartphone — the possibilities are really endless. You’re not just limited to sitting in front of your TV or, if you have kids like I do, playing at your desk. On that second point, I haven’t seen anything too spicy — except for Mandy in a bikini — just yet, but given this is Grand Theft Auto after all, I know it’s coming. I wouldn’t want my son or my wife walking in on something inappropriate on my TV, and by playing with AR glasses on, I don’t have to worry about it.

Industry observers note that now, I know AR glasses, or display glasses, aren’t a must-have gadget like a smartphone, but they make for a very useful accessory. While they’re amazing on planes — and trust me, I’ve put in quite a lot of hours gaming or even watching movies with them aboard an aircraft — they’re just as useful and convenient at home.

As for me, it’s time to get back to Vice City and enjoy the quiet, slow-paced life of Chapter 1 before I eventually have to go pick up Lucia from prison.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Industry observers note that after seven seasons of Star Trek: The Next Generation and a feature film, Dorn joined Star Trek: Deep Space Nine in season 4 as Lt.
  • According to recent reports, appearing on The Show People Podcast to promote Life 2.0, his upcoming movie he wrote, directed, and stars in, Michael Dorn discussed the difference between the "hilarious" Star Trek: The Next Generation set and the "very serious" and "kinda quiet" atmosphere on Deep Space Nine.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Star Trek: Deep Space Nine's set was the opposite of Star Trek: The Next Generation's, Worf actor Michael Dorn confirms.

Industry observers note that after seven seasons of Star Trek: The Next Generation and a feature film, Dorn joined Star Trek: Deep Space Nine in season 4 as Lt. Commander Worf. He found a vastly different environment from TNG's, which was legendary for the cast's camaraderie and hijinks. Dorn played Worf for DS9's remaining four seasons, reuniting with his TNG cast for 1998's Star Trek: Insurrection and 2002's Star Trek: Nemesis.

According to recent reports, appearing on The Show People Podcast to promote Life 2.0, his upcoming movie he wrote, directed, and stars in, Michael Dorn discussed the difference between the "hilarious" Star Trek: The Next Generation set and the "very serious" and "kinda quiet" atmosphere on Deep Space Nine. Read Dorn's quote below:.

Michael Dorn: “It was quite different in a lot of ways from Next Generation. We were a hilarious set. We got the job done, we didn’t waste time, but we were having a great time. The jokes, and the ribbing, and the laughter was all day long. I mean, it was amazing.

Industry observers note that and then you go over to Deep Space, and they’re very serious. It wasn’t bad or people doing stuff, it was just [that] they were serious. It was kinda quiet. ‘Yes, Mr. Brooks, we’re ready for you.’ And I’m going, ‘C’mon guys, let’s…’.

On [TNG], there [wasn’t] anything between the actors, but there [was] definitely relationship stuff between the people in Deep Space. I mean, Armin Shimerman would say that Avery never talked to him. But on the other side, that’s usually the way the business is. [TNG] was an anomaly. It really was.

I’ve worked on a number of series, and people get along, and they have stuff, and they have relationships with each other, and some don’t get along, whatever the case. But that’s just the way it goes. When it’s over, people go their separate ways, and that’s the end of it.”.

Watch Michael Dorn's clip on The Show People Podcast:.

Industry observers note that dorn admits that it's Star Trek: The Next Generation that was the "anomaly" among sets. Countless stories have been told about the chaos and laughter on the TNG set, including wrestling matches between Dorn and the late Patrick Stewart on the USS Enterprise-D's bridge. TNG's cast became a family, and they remain as close today as they were when they forged their bond nearly 40 years ago.

Armin Shimerman backs the serious DS9 set Dorn describes. Armin told The Shuttlepod Show in 2023: "We didn’t laugh… not really… I’m very proud of this, actually: We were there to do the best Star Trek we could possibly do. We took the work very seriously... We worked on our craft and tried to do it as best we could.".

Shimerman also verified what Dorn alluded to: the tone of Star Trek: Deep Space Nine's set was determined by the series lead and number one on the call sheet, Mr. Avery Brooks. "Avery is a very wonderfully serious, charismatic person. And he would laugh, and when he laughed, it was room-filling. But he didn’t laugh that often. And so, we were all very serious-minded.".

There were relationships on DS9, such as Nana Visitor and Alexander Siddig falling in love and marrying in 1997; Nana's pregnancy was even written into the show. Avery Brooks and Cirroc Lofton formed a real-life father-son relationship, while Rene Auberjonois and Armin Shimerman were close, as were recurring guest stars Casey Biggs and Jeffrey Combs, among others.

As Michael Dorn claims, Star Trek: Deep Space Nine's more serious set was more typical of most TV and movie productions. The family that formed on Star Trek: The Next Generation is unique and remains close-knit after the death of Sir Patrick Stewart. Meanwhile, DS9's actors have grown closer after many years of seeing each other on the Star Trek convention circuit.

Star Trek: The Next Generation and Star Trek: Deep Space Nine are streaming on Paramount+.

According to recent reports, anya Taylor-Joy is a fan favorite for playing a variety of roles, be it horror movies like The Gorge, the psychological thriller The Menu, playing Princess Peach in The Super Mario Bros. Movie, or taking over the iconic role of Furiosa in George Miller’s Furiosa: A Mad Max Saga. Later this year, she will appear as Alia Atreides in Denis Villeneuve's franchise capper, Dune: Part 3, starring alongside Timothee Chalamet, Zendaya, and Robert Pattinson.

In her growing filmography, she has already worked with some major directors like George Miller, Doctor Strange’s Scott Derrickson, The Sixth Sense’s M. Night Shyamalan, and more. But before them, Taylor-Joy made her debut with a director who is now well renowned as a modern horror auteur. The filmmaker in question is Robert Eggers, who worked with Taylor-Joy in his directorial debut, The Witch.

According to recent reports, set in 1630s Fresh England, we follow a devout Puritan family banished from their settlement. Now forced to live on a remote farm beside a dark forest, things take a turn when their newborn vanishes while in the care of their eldest daughter, Thomasin. The distraught family descends into paranoia as crop failures and strange occurrences follow. They suspect witchcraft and blame Thomasin for being under the influence of Satan. The movie's simple premise will sit with you only for the first 15 minutes; then the ritualistic isolation will set in.

In a world of suffocating morality and religious paranoia, The Witch examines how fear and dogma can turn a family against itself. With dark forest imagery and oppressive silence, Eggers evokes the emotion of an ancient nightmare. Thomasin’s final transformation leaves you wondering whether she was liberated or damned. But beneath the folklore lie the themes of the fear of female autonomy, forbidden desires, and religious control. The film deliberately leaves room for both; the evil is real and so is religious fanaticism.

Taylor-Joy gives an intense performance as Thomasin, bringing brilliant nuances in her debut role. Ralph Ineson portrays Thomasin’s father, William, with a patriarchal bent of mind and as a man full of fears. Equally impressive is Kate Dickie’s performance as the matriarch of the family, Katherine. The 91% Rotten Tomatoes-rated feature is loved for its gothic atmosphere and physically and emotionally suffocating environment as Eggers delivers a masterclass in slow-building horror. For fans who'd love to check out the film, or discover it, time is right as The Witch is coming to Hulu on December 2, as per ComicBook.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

iOS 27 gave AirPods Pro a variety of newly introduced features, but there’s another addition that’s easy to miss: a convenient new setting in Control Center for Adaptive Audio.

Several AirPods models offer excellent Active Noise Cancellation and Transparency modes—especially AirPods Pro 3 (now only $179).

But Adaptive Audio is another option you may or may not have tried. The feature aims to blend the strengths of both ANC and Transparency in a single mode.

And in iOS 27, Apple added a upcoming setting to let you conveniently fine-tune Adaptive Audio to your preferences.

Industry observers note that while wearing AirPods, open Control Center on your iPhone and tap the volume slider, then hit ‘Listening Mode’ in the bottom-left corner. Here you’ll see the standard listening mode options.

New in iOS 27 though, when ‘Adaptive’ is selected, you can now use a Liquid Glass slider to adjust whether the mode lets in more or less external noise.

Slide it to the left and Adaptive Audio will more closely resemble Transparency, while sliding it to the right makes it cancel out more noise.

You can also move the latest slider incrementally to achieve exactly your ideal balance of Transparency and Noise Cancellation. It’s not limited to just a few preset options.

This Control Center slider is available on all AirPods models that support Adaptive Audio.

Do you ever use Adaptive Audio, and if so, have you adjusted it at all? Let us know in the comments.

#154319. From ‘Disclosure Day’ to ‘Devil Wears Prada’: Emily Blunt Breaks Down 10 of Her Greatest Movie Moments
